title: Northern Vermont Stands Up for Democracy
description:
Can you hear it? The voice of WE THE PEOPLE is growing. 

Around the country people are waking up, showing up, and joining up with their neighbors to rally to protect our Democracy, our Constitution, and our rule of law. The energy of the Hands Off! rallies is now spreading from city centers to other Vermont small towns. 

Beginning May 3rd, join your friends and neighbors right in your community. (St. Albans will gather at Taylor Park, Fairfax will gather at the Fairfax Community Corner Park, Milton will gather on RT 7 in front of Hannafords) Put your own community on this list as well by encouraging your friends and family to come out in your town to Stand Up for Democracy! 

The organization is simple: just gather with others each Saturday in a visible spot in your community from 11:00 to noon to defend our Democracy and civil liberties! Bring your best signs, flags, and energy! These will always be family-friendly peaceful demonstrations. 

Organized jointly by Green Mountain Alliance Indivisible, Rail City Indivisible, and Franklin County Vermont Women for Democracy.

title: Stronger Miami Petition Collecting
description:
Help Make Our Local Democracy More Representative - CALLING ALL MIAMIANS!

It’s time to push forward and  ensure that Miami voters have the voice and representation they deserve. Join Stronger Miami as we collect petitions to create a brighter future for Miami. Stronger Miami’s charter amendment for the City of Miami would: 

•Move city elections alongside statewide elections:
     To increase voter participation, making it easier for working families to take part in our democracy, saving millions of dollars in taxpayer money.

•Expand the City Commission:
     To provide greater representation and ensure every community in Miami has a voice in how our city is run. 

•Ban Commission districts from being gerrymandered:
     To prevent corrupt politicians from abusing the political process for personal gain.

This amendment will make our local elections fairer, more accessible, increase voter participation, and make our city government more reflective of the communities it serves. Collecting signatures is easy, and we’ll make sure you have everything you need to feel confident. Whether it’s your first time or your tenth, we’ve got your back with training, materials, and support. Get involved today and take action to build a Stronger Miami!

title: No Kings Nationwide Day of Defiance with Indivisible Oregon and Partners

location.venue: Salmon Street Springs on Portland Waterfront

description:
On June 14th—Flag Day—Trump is staging a $50 million military parade in D.C., complete with tanks, warplanes, and thousands of troops. While MAGA shows off raw power, they’re slashing Medicaid, food assistance, and other life-saving services. It’s a spectacle meant to intimidate—but we won’t be silent.

Join local Indivisible groups in Portland for NO KINGS—a national day of defiance against authoritarianism and far-right extremism.

We’ll rally at Salmon Street Springs on SW Naito at SW Salmon St., with music, performers, and powerful voices From civil rights to antiwar movements, music has always fueled resistance and brought communities together in protest. After the rally, we’ll take that spirit and join the marchers as they leave the waterfront.

This is a peaceful, nonviolent protest—one rooted in hope, solidarity, and the power of collective action.

NO KINGS IN AMERICA.

title: NO KINGS, but YAAAAS Queen! - Boston Pride
description:
# Join us in joyous defiance of a mad king.

### On June 14th, Mass 50501 and Indivisible Mass Coalition, in partnership with Boston Pride for The People, invite you to dance, sing, and resist with Pride. As our coalition rises to resist tyranny all across America, our Boston LGBTQIA+ community will rise to celebrate resilience in the face of targeted malice and erasure.

We call on all freedom-loving people in Massachusetts to come support a parade dedicated to the resilience of our community at Boston Pride for the People. Bring your Pride flags and signs showing steadfast support for LGBTQIA+ rights and protesting the tyranny of a fascist administration that seeks to erase our communities from public life, American history, and our nation’s future.

## We are here to stay. Joy is our defiance. Pride is our resistance.

Mass 50501 and Indivisible Mass Coalition are official sponsors of Boston Pride 2025. We will have a parade contingent and host a table led by our LGBTQ+ reps at the Pride Festival on Boston Common.

### Schedule
- 11:00 AM: Parade step off from Trinity Church
- 12:30 PM: Arrive at Boston Common
- 12:30 - 3:00 PM: Festival

### Participants are welcome to line up along the parade route. See interactive map [on our website](https://www.mass50501.org/events/june14). 

Please note, marching is not open to the general public, it is for invited members of participating organizations only. 

### Sign Ideas
- No Kings But Drag Kings!
- No Kings But Yaaas Queen!
- Trans Rights Are Human Rights
- Someone I Love Is Trans
- Protect Trans Kids
- Let Trans Kids Play
- Protect Trans Immigrants
- No LGB Without The T

title: Victory Red Day
description:
A campaign for a Day of Female Solidarity and Empowerment on June 24, 2025—the anniversary of Roe v. Wade’s repeal. The idea is simple yet powerful: women and supporters of women everywhere wear red lipstick as a symbol of strength, resilience, and the ongoing fight for gender equality.

Victory Red lipstick has long been a symbol of women’s power, particularly during World War II, when it was worn by women on the home front to represent strength, defiance, and patriotism. During this time, women stepped into roles previously held by men, contributing to the war effort while asserting their independence and resilience. They stood against facism, all while maintaining households and duties outside of their normal realm.

description:
🇺🇸 NO KINGS: A Flag Day Rebellion for Democracy 🇺🇸

In America, we don’t bow to kings. We don’t crown rulers. And we don’t let symbols of freedom become props for power.

This country began with a rebellion against a king. The Revolutionary War was fought to throw off inherited power, unaccountable rule, and the idea that any one man had a divine right to govern others. That spirit—no thrones, no crowns, no kings—is the foundation of our democracy.

On Saturday, June 14—Flag Day—we gather across the country for NO KINGS, a national day of peaceful action. Together, we’re rising up against authoritarianism, corruption, and the growing threats to the freedoms generations have fought to protect.

While the clowniest wannabe oligarch ever throws himself an obscenely expensive military parade in our nation’s capital—surrounded by spectacle, sycophants, and billionaires—WE THE PEOPLE will be highly visible—UNITED as one, demanding that the Constitution be upheld, the scourge REMOVED, the damage REVERSED, and OUR DEMOCRACY RECLAIMED.

We’ve seen what happens when ego replaces leadership, when cruelty is mistaken for strength, and when power is hoarded instead of shared. Enough is enough.

We’re responding with ridicule and humor. Joyful resistance that reflects the absurdity of this political moment and reclaims our country.

Our flag doesn’t belong to strongmen, parties, or movements. It belongs to us—the people. Just like it always has.

title: Wednesday Movement Sign Wave in Lauraville
description:
The Wednesday Movement launched on March 12, 2025 when disgruntled seniors took to the streets in Baltimore to make their feelings known. The Movement, a weekly Pro-Democracy, Anti-Trump, Anti-Putin vigil, gathers on a heavily trafficked Baltimore street corner on Wednesday evenings.

We invite others who feel the same way to join the Movement. You do not need to be old, you do not need to be in Baltimore, and you do not need to stand on Wednesdays, but we ask that you use the Wednesday Movement banner.

It’s easy:​ Reach out to friends and neighbors​. Make some signs (one should say “We Are The Wednesday Movement)​. Pick a day, time, and location that works for your group. And spread the word! title: NO KINGS Vancouver, WA Waterfront
description:
Join us on Saturday June 14th for a powerful day of action at the Vancouver Waterfront!

**Important**: There will NOT be a protest at Esther Short Park. Please help spread the word to avoid confusion.

This peacefule protest will also serve as the official local Women’s March event with the theme “Kicking the Clowns Out” and the motto “The Greatest Sh*t Show on Earth.”

We’ll be marching along the Waterfront, not through downtown (as previously stated), and must follow all city park rules. We will not have electric sound equipment, and speeches will be kept brief with just 2-4 speakers.

**Where to gather**: Meet at the grassy area where concerts are usually held at the Waterfront, across from Evoke Winery and The Crust Collective. 

**Please note**: there is not a lot of shade in this area, so plan accordingly.

To support all participants, marchers with mobility challenges will lead at the front of the march so they are not left behind.

We are encouraging everyone to wear black to help “black out Trump.” and encouraging people to bring noise makers and musical instruments if they want to make noise. Also, since it's flag day bring your respectful flags. 

Parking will be limited. Public transit or carpooling is highly encouraged. C-Van riders can be dropped off near 401 W Columbia Way, at the end of Quayside Place.

We are simplifying the march route to avoid bottlenecks. We will not march over the Grant Street Pier or through the Waterfront Beach Park due to narrow pathways, especially if we have 800+ participants.

Volunteers are still needed for chant leading, media, logistics, safety, crowd counting, ASL interpreting, and more.

We are also looking for:

- Someone with rooftop access at Kirkland Tower to take crowd photos.

- A drone operator to capture aerial shots.

- If you know someone with a sailboat, we’d love to see a sail with “No Kings” displayed!

Momentum matters. In movements, momentum = mass × velocity. Mass is the number of people, velocity is the number of actions. More events helps increase our momentum. The Crowd Counting Consortium (CCC) documents public, visible protests to ensure our efforts are recorded in history.

Let’s help make June 14th a record-breaking day! Ignore counter-protesters and focus on visibility, solidarity, and safety.

Please share this event with your networks, bulletin boards, and friends. 

Let’s show up, be counted, and make history!

Here are links to the flyers if you want to help distribute them:

[Full sheet](https://www.canva.com/design/DAGo39zEz3o/3eZhf6D-rn7fQ0shZtlHkA/edit?utm_content=DAGo39zEz3o&utm_campaign=designshare&utm_medium=link2&utm_source=sharebutton)

[Quarter sheet](https://www.canva.com/design/DAGjtlNZGZQ/aSoECJGQ5xcgIwofx6mSJA/edit?utm_content=DAGjtlNZGZQ&utm_campaign=designshare&utm_medium=link2&utm_source=sharebutton)



We are still in the planning stage of this event so location, time, etc. may change. Please contact us if you want to help with planning this event.   

Saturday, June 14 is a big day. It’s Trump’s birthday, Flag Day and there's a military parade in DC. It’s also a National Day of Action for the 50501 movement and their national sponsors.

Locally, it’s also the Juneteenth Freedom Celebration (10am–3pm) at Esther Short Park and the Pride Block Party (12–7pm) on 7th St between Main Street & Washington St. Both of these events are seeking volunteers.  See below for more information.  

This could be the biggest protest day in U.S. history. The current record holder for largest participation in a single day of protest in the USA is the 2017 Women’s March which had an estimated 4.1 million people. We could beat that if we show up and if we’re counted.

The Crowd Counting Consortium (CCC) is a research group that tracks how many people protest each day in the USA. They only count public protests, and they need proof like public photos, news stories, or social media posts. If we don’t document our actions, we won’t be counted.

For April 5, the Hands Off protests, some online sources said 5.2 million people protested. But the CCC only has information for 1.2 million. That’s a big difference and it’s because not enough groups recorded and reported what how many showed up at their protests.

So for June 14, we need to do better.

Important: Only protest actions count for the CCC. Events like meetings, teach-ins, academic workshops, panel discussions, fundraisers, townhalls, trainings, distribution of mutual aid, petitions, commemorative or celebratory parades, concerts, cookouts, court support, block parties, signature collecting, canvassing activities, or comment sections at government meetings do not count unless they directly disrupt something or clearly protest Trump.

That means the Juneteenth and Pride events don’t count as protests. But we still want to support them and we want to find ways to be counted as protesting Trump too.

[Junteenth Celebration of Freedom](https://www.jfcvancouver.org/)

title: "Moral Monday" Street Rally

address_lines: N. Main St. and W. Division St.

description:
Please join us in opposing cuts to essential safety net programs!

Please join us at weekly recurring  "Moral Monday" street rallies, alternating between Hudson WI and River Falls WI.

Our first “Moral Monday” street rally will be in Downtown Hudson on Monday May 5, from 4PM to 6PM, at the intersection of Second and Vine Streets, where we will hold signs and stand along the public sidewalks.

Our second “Moral Monday” street rally will be in River Falls on Monday May 12, from 4PM to 6PM, at the intersection of Main and Division Streets, where we will hold signs and stand along the public sidewalks.

Folks may join for part or all the two hours, and may bring their own signs or use signs we’ll have to share.

If the weather is bad—hard rain, high wind, and/or lightening—we’ll cancel that week’s rally.

Our "Moral Monday" street rallies are inspired and informed by work of the prominent North Carolina pastor and anti-poverty activist the Rev. William Barber, who founded the Center for Public Theology and Public Policy at Yale and now teaches there.

On the twelfth anniversary of his first "Moral Monday" demonstration, Monday April 28, 2025, Rev. Barber was arrested for praying against the Republican-led budget while in the Rotunda of our US Capitol. At a rally held before he entered the Rotunda to pray, Rev. Barber said: “Forty-three percent of women and almost half of all children are poor and low income. Somebody ought to say something … Somebody gotta challenge this budget.”

We are holding "Moral Monday" street rallies to voice our challenges.

We oppose Republican-approved Congressional budget resolutions that harm the poorest and most vulnerable of Americans in order to give more than $5-trillion in tax breaks to the richest and most privileged of Americans.

We oppose Trump/Musk budget proposals that eliminate or make draconian cuts to federal programs for child care, health research, education, housing assistance, community development, and the elderly.

These funding cuts and proposed budgets are not just public policy choices, they are moral choices. 

These funding cuts and proposed budgets are morally wrong, not just bad public policy choices. 

Please join with us to "say something" and "challenge this budget".

description:

We will gather at Dansbury Park in East Stroudsburg (15 Day Street) at 12:30pm, and start our march to Stroudsburg at 1:30pm.  We will stay on sidewalks, well away from the street, and keep safety first in mind.

The walking distance will be approximately 1.2 miles, so if that presents a challenge, please consider driving instead, and rejoin us on Main Street.

Our event ends as we arrive at the corner of Main Street and Seventh Street in Stroudsburg (around 2:15pm).  After the end of our march, all are invited to join the Juneteenth celebration that will be taking place at Courthouse Square, in a spirit of respect and celebration of the holiday.

The meeting point will be shared at the rally.  And if you know others who are coming, why not carpool with them.

Dansbury Park is off of Day Street, which can be hard to find if you're going north on S. Courtland Street.  As you make a left turn at the light at Washington Street, Day Street is right there between Little Caesars and Rudy's Tavern.

THE NATIONAL ORGANIZERS FOR THIS EVENT ARE ASKING EVERYONE TO PLEASE NOT ATTEND ANY PROTESTS IN WASHINGTON, DC ON JUNE 14TH. PROTEST IN DC ANY OTHER DAY BUT JUNE 14TH. TRUMP WILL SAY PROTESTERS ARE ANTI-ARMY, NOT ANTI-TRUMP. HE WILL ALSO CLAIM PROTESTERS IN HIS CROWD SIZE. WE KNOW SIZE MATTERS TO HIM, SO LET’S SHOW THE WORLD JUST HOW SMALL HE REALLY IS BY NOT CONTRIBUTING TO THAT NUMBER!!!

June 14th is FLAG DAY! The flag doesn’t just belong to Donald Trump and MAGA. It belongs to all of us. We will celebrate "Old Glory", our flag that represents our Democracy, as we claim the Red White and Blue for all!!! We will also celebrate all those who fought for our flag in uniform, our VETERANS, and those who fought on the home front and are still fighting on the home front, our "Angels of Democracy".

In that spirit of celebrating Flag Day, we will have a sing-a-long of “It’s A Grand Old Flag”. In case you have forgotten the lyrics, here they are -

“You're a grand old flag, You're a high flying flag And forever in peace may you wave. You're the emblem of The land I love. The home of the free and the brave. Every heart beats true 'Neath the Red, White and Blue,Where there's never a boast or brag. Should old acquaintance be forgot, Keep your eye on the grand old flag.”

🚨 On June 14th, we’re showing up everywhere he isn’t (we will NOT be in D.C.)—to say no thrones, no crowns, no kings.

It's a good rule of thumb to create signs that do not use sticks or anything else for support that can be perceived as a weapon.✅ Poster Boards and other supplies can be purchased at the Dollar Tree (one of the companies that still has a DEI policy.)

-NO MAD KINGS ALLOWED!!!

-THE PEOPLE UNITED WILL NEVER BE DIVIDED

-WE ARE NOT YOUR PIGGY BANK!

-THE FLAG BELONGS TO ALL OF US

-THANK YOU VETERANS!

-THANK YOU SERVICE MEMBERS!

-PATRIOTS SUPPORT THE V.A.

-AMERICA MADE A PROMISE TO OUR VETERANS WHICH IT NEEDS TO KEEP!!!

-YOU GAVE IT YOUR ALL AND WE THANK YOU!!!

-CELEBRATE OUR VETERANS WHO FOUGHT FOR OLD GLORY!!!

-WE ARE "ANGELS OF DEMOCRACY"

-THIS IS WHAT DEMOCRACY LOOKS LIKE!


COMMUNITY NORMS:

Please read before attending one of our events.

One of our main objectives is to host PEACEFUL, RESPECTFUL and SAFE EVENTS. Remember, when attending a Williamsburg JCC Indivisible event, your actions represent our group, and you are expected to conform to the Community Norms. Safety is a top priority for our attendees. We wish to remind everyone that we do not react to those drivers who make it clear they do not support us by aggravating them through screaming obscenities or making certain hand gestures. We do not want to enrage them and potentially make everyone, including other drivers, less safe. It is easier to wave at everyone and say, “Have a nice day”.

At our events, please do not hold signs or otherwise promote other events that Williamsburg JCC Indivisible is not hosting. You may be placing a potential legal liability onto our group that we are NOT willing to accept.

Please do not engage in DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOURS! If you are asked to stop engaging in activities which are disrupting an event to the point people are complaining to the hosts that they are experiencing physical or emotional trauma, it is expected that you will be respectful of others and follow our Community Norms and stop those behaviours. Loud noises, such as, but not limited to, cowbells, horns, etc., are usually deployed by counter-protesters to disrupt an event, not by attendees participating in an event. If you refuse to disengage from such thoughtless behaviours, do not ruin the event for everyone else - please be kind and leave!

As with our previous events, the same rules apply. We will not engage with counter-protesters. If an issue arises, please notify one of the event organizers. At larger events, these organizers will be wearing Williamsburg JCC Indivisible T-shirts with yellow safety vests. We will not engage in any acts of violence or violation of any applicable laws or engage in civil disobedience. All actions will be peaceful. Everyone participating in this event will be required to behave lawfully to ensure the safety of event participants and will seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. We will obey the orders of authorized event marshals and law enforcement authorities. Event organizers will not be responsible for any injury or damage if any were to occur during this event. Each individual is responsible for the consequences of their actions and attends at their own risk. We will park in the Courthouse parking lot without blocking access lanes and will remove any trash that is left. We are committed to maintaining public health measures to practice safe protesting during these times. Please wear a mask and socially distance if that makes you more comfortable - weigh your own risk in attending. Follow all local safety guidelines at minimum, and any safety instructions from hosts that exceed local law.

✅ Recruit friends → The more people, the more power.✅ Record everything → Post photos/videos with #NoKings ✅

For bridge protests, where visibility from a distance is crucial, the larger the lettering, the better. Here are some key considerations and general guidelines:

General Visibility Rules:

Distance is Key: The primary factor is how far away your audience will be. For highway overpasses, traffic might be moving quickly and at a significant distance.
"Rule of Thumb" for Legibility: A common guideline for outdoor signage is that each inch of letter height provides approximately 10 feet of legibility. So, for every 100 feet of viewing distance, you'd want at least 10-inch tall letters.
Bridge Specifics: Bridges often mean viewing from a greater distance than a sidewalk. Consider vehicles on the road below, and potentially other onlookers further away.
Practical Recommendations for Bridge Protests:

Go Big: Aim for lettering that is at least 12-24 inches tall, and even larger if possible. Some sources suggest using 20x30 or 24x30 inch boards for individual letters to create large, impactful messages.
Bold, Simple Fonts: Choose block, sans-serif fonts (like Arial or Helvetica) that are thick and easy to read. Avoid thin, ornate, or script fonts.
High Contrast Colors: This is critical!
Dark letters on a light background (e.g., black on white, dark blue on yellow) offer the best visibility.
Avoid low-contrast combinations like yellow on white or light blue on a pale background.
Limit your color palette to two or three colors for maximum impact and clarity.
Concise Messaging: Shorter messages with fewer words are easier to read quickly from a distance. Each letter takes up space, so a long message will require smaller letters to fit, reducing visibility.
Material and Construction:
Sturdy materials: Foam core boards or corrugated plastic are more rigid and durable than regular poster board, especially in windy conditions.
Weatherproof: Consider if rain or sun will affect your signs. Paint or vinyl letters are more resilient than marker.
Double-sided signs: If possible, make your signs double-sided to maximize visibility from different angles, especially for media coverage.
Test Your Signs: Before the protest, hold up your signs and have someone view them from a distance similar to what you expect on the bridge. This will help you determine if the lettering is large enough and if the message is clear.
Spacing (Kerning): Ensure there is adequate space between letters and words so they don't blend together from a distance.
By focusing on large, bold, high-contrast lettering and concise messages, you'll maximize the impact and readability of your bridge protest signs.

title: FLAG DAY CELEBRATION - No Kings!
description:
On Flag Day, June 14, while some may focus on a costly and controversial military parade, Traverse Indivisible and Leelanau Indivisible are inviting all members of the community to join a vibrant and inclusive protest and march at The Governmental Center, located at 400 Boardman Ave in Traverse City.

From Noon to 3 PM, this family-friendly celebration will honor the true spirit of Flag Day by bringing people together, fostering community, and providing a platform for voices to be heard.

Program:

Noon to 1pm
-Singing led by TC Sings, with musical backup. This’ll be involving the crowd, so bring your outdoor voices!
-A small number of speakers on the theme of democracy and freedom

1-2:30 pm
-A march on the sidewalks of TC returning to 400 Boardman Ave - bring your family and your dogs. The march is about 1.25 miles long.

2:30-3 pm
Closing remarks and ceremony 

Part march, part protest, this celebration offers a positive and engaging alternative to the military parade in DC that could cost $45 million. Instead of allowing a display of power to be the center of gravity, we want to make action everywhere else the story of America that day. This event is about celebrating in the face of adversity and building community.

Attendees are encouraged to bring their flags, signs, and even costumes to express their patriotism and commitment to democratic values. Whether marching or simply enjoying the festivities, there will be ample opportunities for participation and community connection.

More Information:

This event is part of a larger nationwide movement where activists, alongside local organizers, partners, and leaders from across the pro-democracy and pro-worker movements, will unite for marches, rallies, and demonstrations to reject corrupt, authoritarian politics in the United States.

This demonstration is organized with a steadfast commitment to peace and non-violence. Participants are dedicated to upholding a safe and respectful environment, ensuring all activities remain within the bounds of lawful and peaceful assembly.

title: Indivisible Pittsburgh says: "NO KINGS: Kick Out the Clowns!"
description:
Join INDIVISIBLE PITTSBURGH, B-PEP,  other regional Indivisible groups and community partners as we say: 
“NO Kings–Kick Out the Clowns!” 

Pittsburgh is a democracy town! We know that America is not a country of Kings but of neighbors, building  (I don’t understand this shoulder building) for the future! More than 6,000 Pittsburghers  joined Indivisible Pittsburgh in May to say Hands Off  our rights as Americans and Hands Off of our investments in our future. Join us again  to stand together to say that America is not a country of Kings, but a country of laws. Join us to say that competency matters and that supporting our neighbors is our intention and priority–NOT tax breaks for the wealthy!

For this "No Kings!" event, Indivisible Pittsburgh proudly partners with The Black Political Empowerment Project (B-PEP)  which has empowered African-Americans in their communities since 1986, other local and regional Indivisible groups, and other community organizations.  We will hear from speakers and more at Freedom Corner, just above downtown and then march down to the City-County Building on Grant Street for more speakers, letter writing, and more.   We will join to stand together against Trump, Musk, and Trumpism to say NO to kings, NO to the rich getting richer, NO to oligarchy and YES to Democracy and due process.  


WHAT IS “NO KINGS”?

NO KINGS is a national day of action and mass mobilization in response to the increasing authoritarian excesses and corruption of the Trump administration. We’ve watched as they’ve cracked down on free speech, detained people for their political positions, threatened to deport American citizens, and defied the courts. They’ve done this all while continuing to serve and enrich their billionaire allies. They think they rule—but we are bigger than even their worst aspirations.

Donald Trump is planning a military parade in Washington, D.C. on June 14. This display of might is intended to intimidate opponents and solidify his image as a strongman on our dime—we won’t stand by while that happens.

Instead of allowing this military parade to be the center of gravity, we will make action everywhere else the story of America that day: people coming together in communities across the country to reject strongman politics and corruption.

Alongside local organizers, partners, and leaders from across the pro-democracy & pro-worker movement across the nation, we will demonstrate organized people power that outpaces any authoritarian aspirations.


STATE OF PLAY: WHY WE’RE MOBILIZING JUNE 14 

Donald Trump thinks his rule is absolute, but in America, we don’t do “kings.” Since the inauguration, the Trump administration and its enablers have operated as though they have a mandate—but they don’t, and never did. They are going to extremes to empower Trump and enrich themselves, while cutting jobs and services for the rest of us. Now, they’re turning Flag Day into a celebration of Trump.

💰 He’s using OUR tax dollars to pay for HIS party: Donald Trump’s birthday celebration is expected to cost millions of our tax dollars, all while Republicans claim there’s no money for Social Security, SNAP, or Medicaid.

👑 We are united against kings: Trump has already indicated that he’s aiming for at least a third term, and now he’s planning a self-aggrandizing military parade in D.C But the American people don’t put up with kings. Together, we will mobilize in huge numbers to reject this corruption and abuse of power—it’s in our DNA as a country.

✋ They’ve gone too far: This is bigger than political disagreement. They’ve defied our courts, deported American citizens, disappeared people off the streets, and slashed our services—all while orchestrating a massive giveaway to their billionaire allies. Enough is enough. For anyone who thinks he’s gone too far, this movement is for you.

We’re standing together against the abuses of power, cruelty, and corruption. On June 14, we gather to remind Trump and his enablers: America has No King!



📢 How to Prepare for Your Event:
✅ Bring signs or props → Make your message visible! (Ideas: “NO KINGS IN AMERICA!”, “THE PEOPLE UNITED”, “NOT YOUR PIGGYBANK!”)
✅ Recruit friends → The more people, the more power.
✅ Record everything → Post photos/videos with #NoKings

accessibility_notes:
We have had many people with canes, walkers and wheelchairs on the bridge with us. Please join us

For bridge protests, where visibility from a distance is crucial, the larger the lettering, the better. Here are some key considerations and general guidelines:

**General Visibility Rules:**

* **Distance is Key:** The primary factor is how far away your audience will be. For highway overpasses, traffic might be moving quickly and at a significant distance.
* **"Rule of Thumb" for Legibility:** A common guideline for outdoor signage is that each inch of letter height provides approximately 10 feet of legibility. So, for every 100 feet of viewing distance, you'd want at least 10-inch tall letters.
* **Bridge Specifics:** Bridges often mean viewing from a greater distance than a sidewalk. Consider vehicles on the road below, and potentially other onlookers further away.

**Practical Recommendations for Bridge Protests:**

* **Go Big:** Aim for lettering that is at least **12-24 inches tall**, and even larger if possible. Some sources suggest using 20x30 or 24x30 inch boards for individual letters to create large, impactful messages.
* **Bold, Simple Fonts:** Choose block, sans-serif fonts (like Arial or Helvetica) that are thick and easy to read. Avoid thin, ornate, or script fonts.
* **High Contrast Colors:** This is critical!
    * **Dark letters on a light background** (e.g., black on white, dark blue on yellow) offer the best visibility.
    * **Avoid low-contrast combinations** like yellow on white or light blue on a pale background.
    * **Limit your color palette** to two or three colors for maximum impact and clarity.
* **Concise Messaging:** Shorter messages with fewer words are easier to read quickly from a distance. Each letter takes up space, so a long message will require smaller letters to fit, reducing visibility.
* **Material and Construction:**
    * **Sturdy materials:** Foam core boards or corrugated plastic are more rigid and durable than regular poster board, especially in windy conditions.
    * **Weatherproof:** Consider if rain or sun will affect your signs. Paint or vinyl letters are more resilient than marker.
    * **Double-sided signs:** If possible, make your signs double-sided to maximize visibility from different angles, especially for media coverage.
* **Test Your Signs:** Before the protest, hold up your signs and have someone view them from a distance similar to what you expect on the bridge. This will help you determine if the lettering is large enough and if the message is clear.
* **Spacing (Kerning):** Ensure there is adequate space between letters and words so they don't blend together from a distance.

By focusing on large, bold, high-contrast lettering and concise messages, you'll maximize the impact and readability of your bridge protest signs.

title: NO KINGS East Bay

location.venue: Assemble no later than 12:45 at Wilma Chan Park; march begins at 1pm SHARP!

description:
The narcissist-in-chief is throwing a ridiculous military parade for himself in DC - everywhere else we rise up to say NO KINGS!!

***WATCH THIS SPACE FOR UPDATES!***

*Volunteer Peacekeepers to keep the event safe; ASL interpretation provided; ADA accommodations at Oscar Grant Plaza (special seating up front & keeping ramps clear); porta-potties available.*

**Assemble between 12:30 & 12:45:** Gather at Wilma Chan Park (810 Jackson St.). Parking will be challenging, so take BART to Lake Merritt Station (right next to the Park). **Come early and have lunch in Chinatown!**

**12:45:** March welcome speeches from Oakland City Councilmember Charlene Wang and Stewart Chen, Chinatown Community Leader! Introduced by Elaine Peng, President of Asian Americans for Progressive America!

**1:00 SHARP:** March kicks off! March for 1 mile to Oscar Grant / Frank Ogawa Plaza.

**1:15:** At the Plaza: live music, plus tabling by the orgs co-sponsoring the event!

**2:00:** Rally kicks off! 

MCed by the fabulous Francisco Herrera!

**Confirmed Speakers so far:**

-Representative Lateefah Simon

-Pastor Mike McBride, LIVE FREE USA

-Joe Hawkins, Oakland Pride

-Zahra Billoo, Council on American-Islamic Relations

-Abdi Soltani, ACLU of Nor Cal

-Dan Siegel, activist attorney

-Becca Horwitz, Planned Parenthood

**2:45/3:00-ish** Rally wraps up!

accessibility_notes: This event location is the public plaza in front of Alameda City Hall. The plaza is a flat, paved area. There are a few benches at the location, but if you cannot stand for the duration of your time at the protest, you are welcome to bring a lawn chair or camp chair. Just make sure to set your chair up in an area off to the side, not in the middle, for safety reasons. There is an adjacent bus stop. The closest bathroom facilities are located at the Alameda Free Library at 1550 Oak St (a block away on an adjacent street). Parking will be sparse. Please use ride-sharing or public transit.

title: Join DeKalb Dems at Juneteenth in Stonecrest
description:
The City of Stonecrest is celebrating Juneteenth bigger than ever before this year by hosting it's 3rd annual Juneteenth Celebration of Freedom on Saturday June 14, 2025.

DeKalb Dems will have a visibility tent and we need volunteers to assist with set up and act as Ambassadors who listen to citizen's concerns, offer ways we can support them, and talk about what they can do to safeguard our freedom.

Juneteenth commemorates the effective end of slavery in the United States. Two years after President Lincoln signed the Emancipation Proclamation, news reached Texas and, upon learning they were free, former slaves immediately began celebrating with prayer, feasting, song, and dance. The Juneteenth Celebration of Freedom will celebrate African American culture, heritage, and, most importantly, abolishment of slavery.

The Juneteenth Celebration of Freedom will feature an expanded kidz zone, live performances, food trucks, vendors, and fireworks show. It is a place for all races, nationalities, and religions to join hands and truthfully acknowledge a period in history that shaped and continues to influence our society today, according to a news release. This event is free and open to the public, and we encourage everyone to attend and learn more about the history and culture of Juneteenth!

Please sign up for a shift below and be a part of this Celebration of Freedom.

title: No Kings Day Baltimore
description:
WHAT IS “NO KINGS”?

NO KINGS is a national day of action and mass mobilization in response to the increasing authoritarian excesses and corruption of the Trump administration. 

- We’ve watched as they’ve cracked down on free speech, detained people for their political positions, threatened to deport American citizens, and defied the courts. They’ve done this all while continuing to serve and enrich their billionaire allies. They think they rule—but we are bigger than even their worst aspirations.

- Donald Trump is planning a military parade in Washington, D.C. on June 14. This display of might is intended to intimidate opponents and solidify his image as a strongman on our dime—we won’t stand by while that happens.

- Instead of allowing this military parade to be the center of gravity, we will make action everywhere else the story of America that day: people coming together in communities across the country to reject strongman politics and corruption.

- Alongside local organizers, partners, and leaders from across the pro-democracy & pro-worker movement, we will demonstrate organized people power that outpaces any authoritarian aspirations.

* NO KINGS events should be additive and congruent with adjacent mobilizations and recognitions, including Veterans celebrations, Pride events, and Juneteenth on 6/19.

"NO KINGS DAY” COMES TO WESLEY BOLIN PLAZA – CELEBRATE FREEDOM, FUN & FABULOUSNESS ON JUNE 14TH! Phoenix, AZ – 

Join us for a bold and joyful celebration of freedom, equality, and resistance at No Kings Day on Saturday, June 14th, 2025, from 9:00 AM to 12:00pm at Wesley Bolin Plaza across from the Capitol in downtown Phoenix. This private, permitted event for the whole family. 

Flag Day is all about reclaiming our independence — from oppression, from outdated hierarchies, and from hate — with a vibrant, people-powered event packed with inspiration and fun for the whole family. 

Highlights include: Main Programming (9–11 AM): Hear from local leaders, advocates, and changemakers. Drag Brilliance: Arizona’s best family friendly drag performers will shine between speakers — expect sparkle, sass, and celebration. 

Kid Zone & Carnival Games: Fun for all ages with family-friendly games and activities. Food Vendors offering local favorites and carnival treats. No 
Kings Merchandise Booth to support and fund the event — every purchase helps make this celebration possible. 

We will also be collecting canned and nonperishable food donations for St Mary’s Food Bank; please bring a can or two to support local families in need! 
On-site Port-a-Potties for guest convenience. 

“No Kings Day is more than a protest — it’s a party with a purpose,” said Weird Violet of the Fifty Fifty One Arizona. “We come together to celebrate who we are, support our communities, and imagine a world without Authoritarians, or tyrants.” Join us “We the People” alongside the organizations dedicated to upholding the constitution; 50501 Arizona, Green Party of Arizona, Indivisible, People First Project, Resistance Network of Arizona, Veterans Common Defense, and Women’s March. 

Parking is available surrounding the plaza park, including a limited number of ADA accessible spaces. 

Bring your friends, bring your family, and bring your joy. June 14th at Wesley Bolin Plaza — Let’s build a future with no kings, just people! Social Media Hashtags: #NoKingsDay #NoKingsAZ #DefendDemocracy #DragIsNotACrime

accessibility_notes:
Please join us for our 15th consecutive rally to Defend Democracy in beautiful downtown Bethel. While our overall theme is Defending Democracy, each week we pick a specific focus. On Saturday June 14th, 11am -12:30pm, our focus will be No Kings.  
We are saying NO to authoritarianism. 
We are saying NO to fascism. 
We are saying NO to a dictatorship. 

On June 14th, Flag Day, Donald Trump wants tanks in the street and a made-for-TV display of dominance for his birthday.  A spectacle meant to look like strength.  But real power isn't staged in Washington.   It rises up everywhere else.

No Kings is a nationwide day of defiance.  From city blocks to small towns, from courthouse steps to community parks,  and YES, right here in Bethel's public square, we're taking action to reject authoritarianism, and show the world what Democracy really looks like.

We're not gathering to feed his ego.  We're building a movement that leaves him behind.  The flag doesn't belong to Donald Trump.  It belongs to us and the great ralliers who have been showing up week after week in Bethel for almost 4 months have been carrying and waving flags of all sizes.  The flag belongs to all of us!

We're not watching history happen.  We're making it. On June 14th, we're showing up everywhere he isn't, to say no thrones, no crowns, no kings.  Please join us and help us once again fill up our square.

You will hear a moving poem from local poet laureate, Rick Magee.  

Dr. Carina Bandhauer, Professor of Sociology at Westconn, will discuss the elements of fascism and how Trumps authoritarian actions fit scarily in line with fascism, and what we must do to disallow it.

Dr. Michael Nolan, Professor of History at Westconn,  will discuss the anniversary of another eerily similar military parade also on June 14th, but in 1940, when the German army entered Paris.  He will then discuss the theme of collaboration versus resistance. 

We will then share the story of local resident Alessandra De La Vegas' family.  She has kindly written and audio narrated the personal story of what it was like to live under an authoritarian regime: the Soviet Stalin regime.

Live music will be performed by Pat Stone.
Pat Stone has been performing across Connecticut as a solo artist.  He prides himself on the diversity and unpredictability of his set list.  Pat takes pride in his ability to implicitly know what a particular crowd wants to hear and to give the people what they want.  He has toured nationally with his band “Pat Stone & The Dirty Boots” and was voted ‘Best Americana/Country Artist 2018’ in The Hartford Courant.

The rally is non-partisian. What this means is that like-minded people from diverse backgrounds are participating and are vital to our rallies. Defending Democracy crosses party lines: we have registered Republicans, Unaffiliated, Democrats, and non-voters, all coming together to fight for the rights of “We the People” to determine the type of society we want to live in.

There will be something for everyone. We'll have speakers, we'll rally with our signs, we'll take a short march and we'll have live music. We also like to end each week with a sing-a-long.

A sign-making table will also be available, complete with all the necessary supplies, for young and old to make signs for the rally.

We also collect a non-perishable food item for our local food pantry each week. The food pantry greatly appreciates the donations each week!  Anything you want to contribute is welcome, but some special requests from the food pantry include:

sunscreen

bug spray

Neither can be bought with SNAP but are vital for folks working outdoors in the summer or for kids who will be attending outdoor camps while school is out. Smaller containers that would fit inside a lunchbox are ideal size!

 We are currently lowest on baking supplies, pudding, and jello. Pudding and jello can either be the box mix or predone cups. 

Spices, Coffee and Baking supplies are always needed.

Individually packaged items. If you bought a variety pack of something like granola bars or instant oatmeal and discovered there's a flavor you won't eat, please give us the individual packs out of box.

Empty egg cartons- Any style, so long as they're clean.

SMALL empty detergent bottles

Note: Rally is rain or shine.

There are 2 small benches at the square and we will have a limited number of camping chairs. Please bring your own lawn or camping chair if you'd like.

Approximate Rally Schedule:

10:30 - 11:00 Assemble and rally at curb

11:00 - 11:45 Speaker(s)

11:45 - Noon Rally at curb with chant leader

Noon - 12:20 March with chant leader

12:20   Closing Song

12:30   Disperse

We ask that attendees refrain from sign holding or chanting at the curb during our speaking portion of the rally. We have had issues with speakers being heard because of the increased honking. It also is a courtesy to the speakers who are often discussing serious and sensitive topics. We are sharing a small square so we need your help to make the rallies comfortable for everyone.

We have tried to arrange the rallies so there is a little something for everyone: chanting, marching, themes with speakers, live music, fun trinkets, sign making. We appreciate every one of you that attends and we are working hard to bring all of us together to voice our frustrations, build community and also hopefully learn a little something from experts or your fellow neighbors experiences.

We appreciate your understanding and cooperation. ❤️

We also ask that you park at one of the four public parking lots.   The lot that is very close to the rally location, PT Barnum Square,  is behind the municipal center (number 1 on the map that will be emailed after you register).  PT Barnum Square is the triangle shaped area to the far right on the map and in the center of the map. 

Although all street parking is public, we ask that you please do not park in the limited parking spots in front of our local businesses, but definitely enjoy our beautiful towns restaurants and shops after the rally! 
Thank you 😊
(I will email the map to you after you register)

 Let’s Chalk up the roads of our town with “No Kings” messages!!  
We will meet at Meckauer park at 10 AM, on Friday to chalk and then disperse to chalk around town afterwards. (BYO chalk- we will have some on hand). 
Anyone who cannot make it Friday can chalk messages when and where they can. 
 Let’s spread the “No Kings” message through chalk!  (Please use washable chalk).

title: #NoKings Day with Sister District Project SF
description:
Join your friends and neighbors at Sister District Project San Francisco for the #NoKings mass protest and day of defiance!

On June 14, rise up with millions across the country, on Tr*mp's planned military parade day, to stand in opposition and fight back against the attacks on our freedoms by this jury-determined rapist, twice-impeached, 34-time convicted felon, and January 6 traitor. 

Look for the Sister District San Francisco banner on the sidewalk in front of Children's Day School (601 Dolores St), directly across from Dolores Park at the corner of 19th St. We will meet there at 11am before the march down Market Street that heads to the main rally in front of City Hall. 

Bring signs, wear your SDP t-shirt and caps if you have them (we'll have a few extras). 

Together, let's demand a country that puts our families over billionaires' fortunes—public schools over private profits, healthcare over hedge funds, prosperity over the profits of price-gouging and climate polluting corporations.

_A core principle behind all #NoKings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values._

To learn more about this national day of action, visit [nokings.org](https://www.nokings.org/)

To learn more about Sister District Project, visit [SisterDistrict.com](https://sisterdistrict.com/strategy).

Since 2016, Sister District Project has been building enduring progressive power in the states to improve people's lives, including by supporting community-based organizations led by people of color on the ground, like [New Virginia Majority](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sd016-va-nvmef-sf), who do critical grassroots work year round.

You are welcome to join any of our monthly meetings, whichever is most convenient for you! 

We host events on **Zoom the first Tuesday** of each month; in-person **Happy Hours on the first Thursdays** of even-numbered months; in-person **Coffee Hours on first Thursdays** of odd-numbered months (locations vary); or in-person **Postcard events** on third Sundays or Mondays.

## In America, we don’t put up with would-be kings. ##

### 🤝 On Saturday, June 14, join [OC Indivisible Coalition](https://linktr.ee/ocindivisiblecoalition), [50501 Movement Orange County](https://linktr.ee/50501oc), [Women's March OC](https://www.womensmarch.com/), [WAVE](https://www.wave4all.org/), and other community partners as we gather in solidarity to uphold our Constitution, support our communities and say NO KINGS in America. ###

NO KINGS is a national day of action and mass mobilization in response to increasing authoritarian excesses and corruption from Trump and his allies. We’ve watched as they’ve cracked down on free speech, detained people for their political views, threatened to deport American citizens, and defied the courts. They’ve done this all while continuing to serve and enrich their billionaire allies and attack our most vulnerable populations.

🇺🇸 The flag doesn’t belong to Donald Trump. It belongs to us. We’re not watching history happen. We’re making it.

**On June 14th, we’re showing up everywhere he isn’t—to say no thrones, no crowns, no kings.**

Check out [nokings.org](https://www.nokings.org/) for more information.

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to peaceful, nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

📢 How to Prepare for **NO KINGS OC**:

✅ Bring signs or props → Make your message visible! (Ideas: “NO KINGS IN AMERICA!”, “THE PEOPLE UNITED”, “NOT YOUR PIGGYBANK!”)

✅ Recruit friends → The more people, the more power.

✅ Record everything → Post photos/videos with #NoKingsOC


🚨 We’re fighting for democracy. Let’s make them listen.

title: NO KINGS Newark DE

address_lines: South College Avenue & West Main Street

description:
Get ready for a big day of national protest on June 14th! A parking map is available at www.IndivisibleNewarkDE.org. Please be conscious of where you park, and leave closer spots for people who use a wheelchair, a walker, etc. 

We are coordinating a food drive at this protest to support the Delaware Food Bank! Look for the black pickup truck with the Food Bank signs right at S College and W Main!

There is an optional 1.5 mile march. Anyone who does not want to march can remain at the protest start location throughout.

description:
This is a local Indivisible event!

Avelo Airlines has accepted a $150 million contract to operate deportation flights, aiding in the illegal removal of individuals without their right to a fair hearing or due process. This is not only inhumane but a direct violation of our Constitution.

We’re calling for a full boycott of Avelo Airlines and organizing weekly protests at our local airport.

We will be on the sidewalk leading to the Charles M. Schulz Sonoma County Airport, which is currently a hub for Avelo's flights. At a time when a maximum number of travelers will see our protest, it is also a good opportunity to protest federal layoffs with the FAA.

You can park nearby or take SMART to get there (except 5/31). Do not park in private lots.

NO PROTEST ON JUNE 1st. Sunday's, 11-2pm, resume on June 8th.

title: Croton, NY: Pass a Resolution Against Project Maple
description:
**Join us outside the Croton Board of Trustees meeting to demand local action against Project Maple** — a dangerous fracked gas pipeline expansion plan that threatens our climate, our river, and our health.

Fossil Fuel company Enbridge's Project Maple would expand the amount of fracked gas running through the existing Algonquin Pipeline (which runs through Westchester County) by replacing existing pipe and expanding compressor stations. 

This project would lock us into decades of fossil fuel dependence — just when we need to be transitioning to clean energy. It’s risky, unnecessary, and completely out of step with New York’s climate goals. **Croton has the chance to be a climate leader by passing a resolution opposing this reckless project.**

Meet us outside Croton-on-Hudson Village Hall, where we’ll rally together, then head into the board meeting to make powerful public comments demanding the Village take a stand.

Let’s pack the room and show our elected officials that Croton stands for climate justice, not fossil fuel expansion. Bring your friends, your voice, and your passion — we’ll have talking points and signs ready to go!

title: NO KINGS Frisco, Texas

location.venue: FM 423 (both sides) between Main/King and Stonebrook

description:
June 14th is Flag Day and the 250th anniversary of the establishment of the United States Army. Coincidentally, it is also President Trump’s 79th birthday, and he is staging a $45 million military parade to appease his ever expanding ego! 

Who does that? Kings, tyrants, and dictators do.

In 1775, we began the fight for independence from the tyrant King George III of England. In 2025, we are reminding Trump and our elected representatives that America rejects his authoritarian actions, consolidation of power, disregard of law, and defiance of the courts. WE THE PEOPLE proclaim, once again: NO KINGS!  

We are joining millions of people all over the nation to rain on his taxpayer funded parade. We are reclaiming the flag and honoring those who have died protecting the democratic principles it represents. We are preserving our constitutional democracy. We are asserting the Army’s motto: THIS WE’LL DEFEND! 

NO KINGS is a national day of action that welcomes people from all walks of life to join in peaceful, joyful, nonviolent dissent. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

WHAT TO BRING: a friend, water, US flags, signs that reflect our theme - no kings, Army motto, democracy, rule of law, etc.

WHAT TO WEAR: sunscreen, light-colored clothing and hat, patriotic colors, stars & stripes, Army shirts, camoflage, Revolutionary War costumes, etc.

SPECIAL REQUEST: I’m looking for people that could bring the painting “The Spirit of ’76” to life. For that, we need a piccolo player playing “Yankee Doodle” and/or “The Army Goes Rolling Along,” a snare drummer, and a flag bearer. I’m also looking for trumpeters to play “The Star-Spangled Banner” and/or some bugle calls. Please contact me if you can help with this!

description:

Schedule:

- 2 PM:  Rally 

- 3 PM: March (Time subject to change) 
  
After the march, return to Kiener Plaza for community resource information.

Donald Trump thinks his rule is absolute, but in America, we don’t do “kings.” Since the inauguration, the Trump administration and its enablers have operated as though they have a mandate—but they don’t, and never did. They are going to extremes to empower Trump and enrich themselves, while cutting jobs and services for the rest of us. Now, they’re turning Flag Day into a celebration of Trump. 

We’re standing together against the abuses of power, cruelty, and corruption. On June 14, we gather to remind Trump and his enablers: America has No King!

Join millions nationwide on June 14 to march against authoritarian politics and billionaire takeover. Be part of a national moment that changes the conversation—and turns the tide.

Register to receive details and updates in the days leading up to the event.

title: NO KINGS Charlotte: Naked Emperor Rally and March
description:
## “No Kings” coalition together with “Kick Out The Clowns” presents: Naked Emperor Rally and March! 

Join us for an event to remember as we join forces with multiple partners to make some noise in Charlotte. Let’s show that this would-be emperor truly wears no clothes by joining this nationwide protest rejecting authoritarianism, billionaire-first politics, and the militarization of our democracy.

**Due to overwhelming interest in this event, we will now be gathering at First Ward Park for the 11:00 rally,** where we'll listen to community speakers and then march through Uptown Charlotte! The March route is approximately 1.4 miles. Join us for the rally, the march or both.

Due to limited free parking in the area, **we are encouraging attendees to use Lynx light rail to arrive at this event. The closest stop is 7th Street Station, a short walk from the park.** There are several paid parking decks in the vicinity with 7th Street Station Parking Garage being the closest with handicapped parking. Additional portable restrooms will be present at the park for our event.

We are partnering with Drumstrong to provide rhythm and drums for encouragement and support during our march, and we will be offering some additional noise makers to you to use. Does your group have an interest in adding theater and/or excitement to the day? Reach out to us at indivisibleclt@gmail.com to coordinate additional partnerships!

*We are committed to nonviolent action, and we expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with us. Signs and chants must not incite violence, and signs may not portray swastikas in any form. While there is always an inherent risk to protesting, we are encouraging a family friendly event.*

Please bring water bottles, any snacks you may need and remember to wear your sunscreen! Additional water and snacks will be available along with a first aid station. Marshals in neon vests will be available to answer your questions or assist along the way.

title: NO KINGS Carroll County, MD
description:
# 🚨PLEASE NOTE: WE WIL ***NOT*** BE MARCHING FOR THIS EVENT 

The original plan was to march through downtown Westminster, but a different event will be taking place in downtown Westminster at the same time as ours, so we will NOT be able to march there. We will instead GATHER AND STAY AT THE COMMISSIONERS BUILDING at 225 N. Center St., Westminster, where we will have the band The Good Trouble Troubadours perform, and several community members speak about their experiences being impacted by this administration's overreach. We apologize for the confusion and plan on marching at a future date. Thank you!

**On June 14th, we’re showing up everywhere he isn’t—to say no thrones, no crowns, no kings.** For this event we will gather at the County Commissioners building (which is ADA compliant) to protest, connect, dance to some great music by The Good Trouble Troubadours, and hear some of our neighbors' experiences with this Administration's unconstitutional and criminal overreach.

What do we want? ELECTED LEADERS!
When do we want them? NOW and always because the United States is a democracy--it's not a monarchy, it's not an oligarchy, and it's not a dictatorship. It's not run by a king and his henchmen, it's *led* by *elected* individuals in service to the American people.

NO KINGS is a national day of action and mass mobilization in response to increasing authoritarian excesses and corruption from Trump and his allies. We’ve watched as they’ve cracked down on free speech, detained people for their political views, threatened to deport American citizens, and defied the courts. They’ve done this all while continuing to serve and enrich their billionaire allies.


🚨**On Saturday, June 14, we’re taking to the streets nationwide. We’re not gathering to feed his ego. We’re building a movement that leaves him behind.**🚨


The flag doesn’t belong to Donald Trump. It belongs to us. We’re not watching history happen. We’re making it.


**On June 14th, we’re showing up everywhere he isn’t—to say no thrones, no crowns, no kings.**
For this event we will gather at the County Commissioners building (which is ADA compliant), march through downtown Westminster (the path we take is not guaranteed to be accessible; we estimate it will take about 20 minutes), and re-convene at the Commissioners building to continue our protest and connect with each other. **If you are not able to march you can stay at the Commissioners building and we'll meet you back there!**

Check out nokings.org for more information.

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

title: Public Service Commission Candidate Open Forum
description:
As temperatures heat up and power bills rise, frustrated Georgians are starting to look at the Public Service Commission (PSC) for new regulations and to potentially bust up a Georgia Power monopoly.  Statewide PSC primaries for seats in Districts 2 and 3 will be held on June 17 and the general election will be on November 4.

[Coastal Georgia for Democracy](https://www.coastaldemocracy.org/), the Savannah Indivisible group for Georgia District 1, will host a live open forum for voters to ask the candidates questions about their positions in advance of the election. The event will be held at the [Coastal Georgia Center](https://maps.app.goo.gl/nvQiVJN95jvp4VSKA), 305 Fahm Street, Savannah, on June 12 at 6:00pm. The free event is open to the public.

All PSC candidates have been invited to appear and will answer voters’ questions regarding anything under the purview of the Public Service Commission, which includes how much Georgia residents pay for their electricity, landline telephones, and natural gas.  They also oversee the 811 “Call before you dig” line and items related to line interruptions when they are improperly monitored by contractors and residents. 

Confirmed attendees for the candidate forum include Dr Alicia Johnson in District 2 and Daniel Blackman, Peter Hubbard, Robert Jones, and Keisha Sean Waites in District 3.
 
The Georgia Public Service Commission has exclusive power to decide what are fair and reasonable rates for services under its jurisdiction. They must balance Georgia citizens' need for reliable services and reasonable rates with the need for utilities to earn a reasonable return on investment while not guaranteeing it. The Commission protects consumers' interests while abiding by legal standards in setting rates. All matters scheduled for public hearing are heard by the Commissioners or in special cases, by an appointed hearing officer in open session. Read more [about the PSC and this election](https://www.coastaldemocracy.org/the-2025-ga-psc-special-election).

Coastal Georgia for Democracy, a grassroots group of residents in the coastal Georgia region, is Savannah’s Indivisible group in Georgia’s District 1. We are committed to protecting democracy and promoting genuine equity and inclusion through progressive advocacy. We do not endorse candidates. We aim to defend and protect against attacks on constitutionally guaranteed freedoms, including safe and fair elections and the voting rights of citizens. To learn more, visit us at https://www.coastaldemocracy.org.

title: No Kings-National Day of Action Rally
description:
On June 14, from 11:00am- 1:30pm we will gather at the intersection of US-1 & SR-520, Cocoa, FL to remind Trump and his enablers: America has No King!
🔘Please bring your own beverages & signs.
🔘There will be some signs, sign making materials & water provided.
🔘Feel free to dress in costumes.
🔘Music & street theater throughout gathering.
🔘This is a Peaceful gathering. Please ignore any distractors, use crosswalks, & stay on sidewalks. There will be safety people in vests on all 4 corners.
‼️➡️Since many food pantries & shelters are taking financial hits, WE ARE DOING A FOOD & SUPPLIES DRIVE on the SW corner-
If you're able, please bring non-perishable food, blankets, socks, etc. to donate.⬅️‼️
Donald Trump thinks his rule is absolute, but in America, we don’t do “kings.” Since the inauguration, the Trump administration and its enablers have operated as though they have a mandate—but they don’t, and never did. They are going to extremes to empower Trump and enrich themselves, while cutting jobs and services for the rest of us. Now, they’re turning Flag Day into a celebration of Trump.
💰 He’s using OUR tax dollars to pay for HIS party: Donald Trump’s birthday celebration is expected to cost millions of our tax dollars, all while Republicans claim there’s no money for Social Security, SNAP, or Medicaid.
👑 We are united against kings: Trump has already indicated that he’s aiming for at least a third term, and now he’s planning a self-aggrandizing military parade in D.C But the American people don’t put up with kings. Together, we will mobilize in huge numbers to reject this corruption and abuse of power—it’s in our DNA as a country.
✋ They’ve gone too far: This is bigger than political disagreement. They’ve defied our courts, deported American citizens, disappeared people off the streets, and slashed our services—all while orchestrating a massive giveaway to their billionaire allies. Enough is enough. For anyone who thinks he’s gone too far, this movement is for you.
We’re standing together against the abuses of power, cruelty, and corruption.
When clowns 🤡 are elected, expect a circus 🎪 -
America 🇺🇸 has No King! 👑

This a local Indivisible event!

While some in DC are hosting a massive, wildly expensive, taxpayer-funded display of US military might in DC to humor the ego of an aspiring authoritarian, here in the Waterville, Maine, area Indivisible Mid Maine will host a non-violent march and rally to celebrate and communicate the values and joys of the compassionate, sustainable, just community, country, and world we are striving to build. Join us!

This non-violent community event will consist of a march AND a rally. Participants are welcome to join us for any portion of the event. If you want to and are able to march, join us at 10 am at the town office in Fairfield, Maine, (19 Lawrence Ave.) with upbeat signs you can carry. At the Fairfield Town Office we will hear a very brief statement, reminding us all of the civil and human rights and values that are enshrined in both the Maine and US Constitutions and which we urge our leaders to uphold.

Marchers will then head down Lawrence Ave. to Main St., turn right and march along Main Street till it becomes College Ave. and then march along College Ave. until it becomes Main St., in Waterville, all the way to Waterville City Hall (1 Common St.). There the same brief statement that was delivered at the Fairfield Town Office will be repeated. We expect to arrive at City Hall around 11:30.

The distance of the march is about 3.4 miles, flat and with sidewalks all or most of the way. Participants should feel free to participate in any portion of the march, or the whole thing. Folks who want to travel the route by car or other vehicle are welcome to do so while we are marching, and may want to decorate their vehicles with signs similar to those that the marchers will be carrying.

After the march, participants will gather at a nearby location (TBD!) where the associated rally will begin at 11:30 and run until about 1pm, with music, light snacks, opportunities to meet and talk with others who share our non-violent, pro-democracy, pro-justice and human rights values, and to make and display relevant signs, etc.

Our goal is to continue building community here where we live, even as we engage in resistance against the larger forces that seek to destroy everything we hold dear. Please join us for all or part of this fun and uplifting event. If you can help with any of the pieces of the event, please reach out. And please watch this space for updates!

title: 12 Days to Democracy! JOIN THE MARCH - June 16 to 28

location.venue: Dilworth Park, City Hall, Philadelphia, PA

description:
Democracy has always been about the power of the people. It’s we, the people, who will fight the fight for a more just and equitable society.

This is the work– not of kings– but by all of us and for all of us. We’re the ones who have to travel the distance.

And this is why, at this critical juncture in our history - when the laws and institutions protecting our right to fight are under attack like never before - we have decided to take a very long walk.

Our walk – a 120-mile journey from Philly to DC - will take us through towns, into cities, and along the trails of the East Coast Greenway, and we hope that it will look like the world we want to see: friendly and civil. Open to the joys of human variation and the friendliness of flexible minds. This is a big, long mission; a walk/march, inspired by the big, hopeful, goodness-based, law-governed dream that is American democracy. We hope you’ll consider joining us - for a mile, a city limit, the whole journey.

title: NO KINGS South Bay LA
description:
June 14, 1775 marked the birth of the U.S. Army—a force created to stand against tyranny and unchecked power. Now, 250 years later, that legacy is being distorted. President Donald Trump plans to commemorate the Army’s anniversary with a taxpayer-funded military parade in Washington, D.C.—on his own birthday. This **$45 million spectacle** isn’t just about the military; it’s about glorifying one man.

Trump has made flirtatious comments about seeking a third term, hinting at constitutional workarounds, though he officially claims he’ll be a two-term president. Regardless, the ambition is clear—and dangerous. This isn’t how democracies are supposed to work. **On June 14th, we’re showing up everywhere he isn’t—to say no thrones, no crowns, no kings.** NO KINGS is a National Day of Action and mass mobilization. Check out nokings.org for more information.

His administration continues to dismantle democratic norms:

- Immigration authorities have fast-tracked deportations, in some cases defying due process protections and alarming rights groups

- Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has launched an unfounded investigation into autism’s causes, reviving debunked theories linking it to vaccines—causing distress among scientists and disability advocates

- Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility (DEIA) programs are under attack. For example, the NIH has withheld medical research funding for universities if they do not dismantle their DEIA initiatives.

- Institutions like Columbia University and Harvard have faced federal funding cuts and pressure to suppress campus protests, raising serious concerns about free speech and academic freedom.

- Trump’s proposed budget slashes education, Medicare, and Medicaid—gutting essential services while greenlighting a vanity parade.

**South Bay LA** stands for truth over theatrics. Every peaceful protest is a defense of democracy and dignity. If you believe Trump has gone too far, this movement is for you. Join the South Bay community's rebuttal to Trump's show of undesired authoritarian power. Show that American pride is rooted in diversity, equity, inclusion—and the fundamental belief that people with disabilities are not broken, but that there is ability in every disability.

🚨**On Saturday, June 14th we are rallying at Torrance City Hall with a clear message: One Nation, Indivisible with Truth and Justice for All.  #NoKings** 🚨

_**A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.**_

title: Protect Social Security Rally and protest, Tuesdays, 5/13 to 8/26/2025 @11:30AM
description:
Members from CBFD Indivisible, Neighbors in Action and others,  invite you to join  a weekly  “Hands Off Social Security" rally every Tuesday from  11:30 AM-12:30 PM at the La Mesa Social Security office, 7961 University Avenue.

Participants gather at 11:30 AM for a one hour protest.  

Bring your signs in support of Social Security, and make sure to bring a hat, and your own water. We’ll be on the sidewalk in a relatively sunny location, so that hat will make a big difference.

As with all rallies and protests, we support peaceful protest and believe that educating the public via protests works best when we are respectful and positive.

Please do not park in the Social Security lot. 

See you on Tuesdays in La Mesa, CA.  11:30 AM to 12:30 PM.  Let’s make it known that we won’t stand by while the most successful program in our nation’s history is decimated by The Trump regime just so they can give big tax breaks to further enrich the ultra-wealthy.

description:
Thousands of people are expected to rally on June 14 to make clear that we are not on board with what is happening to our country. Many of these people will be fired up to take action, but not know where to turn to make a meaningful difference beyond demonstrating. This is where you come in!

title: Sound the Alarm for Democracy

description:
***If you are not from Terre Haute, Please start one of these near you! We would love this to be Nationwide!!!***

The Trump Administration and Elon Musk are acting with selfishness, hiding their actions in cowardice, and systematically dismantling the values upon which our country was built. JOIN US EVERY MONDAY!!
SOUND THE ALARM FOR DEMOCRACY

title: Kings & Clowns Rally

address_lines: South Oneida Avenue & East Kemp Street

description:
When a Clown moves into a Palace, he doesn’t become a King, the Palace becomes a Circus. While the clown throws himself a birthday party in Washington, the people in the Northwoods are defending our democracy!


WHAT IS “NO KINGS! NO CLOWNS!? It is a national day of action and mass mobilization in response to the increasing authoritarian excesses and corruption of the Trump administration. We’ve watched as they’ve cracked down on free speech, detained people for their political positions, threatened to deport American citizens, and defied the courts. They’ve done this all while continuing to serve and enrich their billionaire allies. They think they rule—but we are bigger than even their worst aspirations.
Donald Trump is planning a military parade in Washington, D.C. on June 14. This display of might is intended to intimidate opponents and solidify his image as a strongman on our dime—we won’t stand by and watch!
Donald Trump thinks his rule is absolute, but in America, we don’t do “kings.” Since the inauguration, the Trump administration and its enablers have operated as though they have a mandate—but they don’t, and never did. They are going to extremes to empower Trump and enrich themselves, while cutting jobs and services for the rest of us. Now, they’re turning Flag Day into a celebration of Trump.
💰 He’s using OUR tax dollars to pay for HIS party: Donald Trump’s birthday celebration is expected to cost millions of our tax dollars, all while Republicans claim there’s no money for Social Security, SNAP, or Medicaid.
👑 We are united against kings: Trump has already indicated that he’s aiming for at least a third term, and now he’s planning a self-aggrandizing military parade in D.C But the American people don’t put up with kings. Together, we will mobilize in huge numbers to reject this corruption and abuse of power—it’s in our DNA as a country.
✋ They’ve gone too far: This is bigger than political disagreement. They’ve defied our courts, deported American citizens, disappeared people off the streets, and slashed our services—all while orchestrating a massive giveaway to their billionaire allies. Enough is enough. For anyone who thinks he’s gone too far, this movement is for you.
We’re standing together against the abuses of power, cruelty, and corruption. On June 14, we gather to remind Trump and his enablers: America has No King!
Whether you're outraged by attacks on civil rights, skyrocketing costs, abductions and disappearances, the gutting of essential services, or the assault on free speech—this moment is for you. Whether you've been in the fight for years or you're just fed up and ready to take action—this moment is for you!
 He’s using OUR tax dollars to pay for HIS party.
Donald Trump’s birthday celebration is expected to cost millions of our tax dollars, all while Republicans claim there’s no money for Social Security, SNAP, or Medicaid.

Together, we will mobilize in huge numbers to reject this corruption and abuse of power—it’s in our DNA as a country.
They’ve gone too far.
This is bigger than political disagreement. They’ve defied our courts, deported American citizens, disappeared people off the streets, and slashed our services—all while orchestrating a massive giveaway to their billionaire allies. Enough is enough. For anyone who thinks he’s gone too far, this movement is for you.
The Army’s birthday isn’t about parades or pageantry — it marks the beginning of America’s rejection of kings.
On June 14, 1775, the Continental Congress created the U.S. Army to stand up against a monarch who claimed absolute power. 250 years later, Donald Trump wants to twist that legacy into a personal celebration of himself.
That’s why we say: No Thrones. No Crowns. No Kings. No Clowns!
No Kings no clowns is about defending the ideals they fought for. This country doesn’t belong to strongmen. It  belongs to us!

title: We The People Wednesdays in Walnut Creek
description:
This is a local Indivisible event organized by Indivisible ReSisters Contra Costa!  Join us every Wednesday evening from 5-6 p.m. at the corner of Ygnacio Valley Road and Civic Drive for a rousing honk and wave visibility action.  Bring your signs and raise your voice for democracy and to protect our rights!  

This is a nonviolent event. Stay within your rights, don’t break laws, stay safe, stay peaceful, and avoid any risk you don’t feel comfortable with. There are several parking lots within walking distance or you can find street parking at Civic Park or on Civic Drive or Arroyo Way.

title: "No Kings In America"

description:
