title: We Have No Kings In America!
description:
On Flag Day, June 14, 2025 in Dripping Springs, at 10 am, we shall once again gather under the big oaks at the picnic tables at Veterans Park in Downtown Drippin' to exercise our First Amendment Rights.

In light of the fact that "someone" is having a big, unAmerican and very expensive military parade in D.C. that same day, we are going to celebrate our flag and our freedom in our own way, with signs, banners, FLAGS and our cars, painted up like it's Prom Night.  

Our celebration of Freedom and our Rights as Americans will begin, as it does every Saturday morning, with a march to the intersection of RR 12 and Hwy 290 West, to OCCUPY the four corners with our signs and flags flying, while we wave to our neighbors passing by.  

We will also be handing out pocket-sized copies of the U.S. Constitution, just in case some of our neighbors would like to compare what is going on these days, with what the Founding Fathers had in mind.

We have been greeted most Saturdays by friendly waves, thumbs up and honks, but there are always a few who for some reason think we should not be expressing ourselves.  We wave and smile at them, too!

Then, around noonish, we will once again gather under the oaks to organize ourselves into a caravan of cars and trucks, flying our flags, and adorn our vehicles with white shoe polish in the time-honored tradition of Prom Night, weddings and winning the State Championship.  

We will do a little dance around town, our very own version of a Flag Day Parade, then making our way to one of the local watering holes to hoist a cold one, and get some lunch.  Stay tuned for details.

title: Of the People, By the People, For the People - March and Rally
description:
From the same crew who organized the April 5th rally, join us June 14 for a national day of protest as Americans across the country unite in support of Liberty for All! This local Indivisible event is the official June No Kings rally, organized by Flathead Democracy and 50501MT. Other registered events are a good pre-party but aren't authorized by our team.

Title: Of the People, By the People, For the People- Protest March and Rally

Theme: Attack Our Problems, Embrace Our Neighbors

Diversity makes our nation stronger! Division is our weakness, and the Mega Rich Oligarchs know it. Join us, the 99%, to condemn federal attacks on and show our appreciation for foreign students, immigrants, the LGBTQIA+ community, Native Americans, Black Americans, Latino Americans, Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders, working poor, homeless, those on disability, veterans, the elderly, federal workers and more. The time to speak up is NOW!!! No more parties, no more politics, no kings. The time to stand up is NOW! Someone you care about is already affected. Who will be next?

Where and When:
March Route- Meet at 3:30 pm on either side of the old Flathead County Courthouse (800 S Main St, Kalispell). Rally at Depot Park @4-5:30 pm.

We will proceed along both sides of Main Street to Depot Park. We’ll be walking on the sidewalks so please make sure there’s a space for people who aren’t protesting to pass. We also need to follow all traffic laws, no blocking traffic, obeying crosswalk lights, and staying on the sidewalk.

If you can’t walk from the courthouse, there will be a crew at Depot Park for the duration of the event so plan to stay there.

Rally Details- The rally ends at Depot Park in Kalispell! This is where we’ll have speakers, music, and food (more on that later) from 4-5:30 pm. After the rally, you can stay and visit or walk back to the courthouse at your leisure.

Safety notes: There will likely be a few counter protesters, although we’ve taken steps to minimize this risk. Please just ignore them. There will be a few folks on hand to help deescalate potential conflicts but since there will be so many of us, it’s helpful if we commit to supporting one another and NOT engaging with trolls.

We’ll be in Depot Park so do your best to tread lightly on the grass and to clean up. This is our chance to demonstrate that we’re a respectful and upstanding group–neighbors and friends who are standing up for our country.

Parking and bathrooms: There’s parking on the east and west sides of the old courthouse and in the surrounding neighborhoods. If you’re meeting at Depot Park, you can park at the Mall or the Super 1. Please only park in the Depot Park parking lot if you are elderly or disabled.

Depot Park bathrooms will be available!

Food: We will have a drink and food table with “Resistance Swag” and voter registration at Depot Park. If you would like to donate drinks, side dishes or desserts, please drop them off at Depot Park at 3:00 pm. If you know any businesses that might want to donate and you can reach out and coordinate we’d appreciate it! Thanks in advance!

These notes are also important!

Email flatheaddemocracy@gmail.com with questions or if you're interested in volunteering for logistics or donating food/supplies!

Bring cash! We’ll have a table setup for some swag and appreciate donations to cover printing costs, as well as the event permit and sound system. We’re going old school on this one and will have a donation jar. Even a couple bucks helps cover costs.

Please bring a poster (or more!) sharing what group of people you are most passionate about protecting or how diversity makes us stronger. We will have some poster making materials at the beginning if you can’t, but they will be limited. If you have extra materials to share that’s helpful too!

Wear red, white, and blue to demonstrate solidarity. This isn’t a must but it makes for a really impressive visual!

Thank you for reading all this to help us prepare together and get pumped! We are making history together ✊🏽

Best, The Whole Flathead Democracy Team

title: NO KINGS! "We the People" Democracy Fair [Palo Alto]
description:
**This Flag Day, join us for a democracy fair.**
Following a day of peaceful protests held in counterpoint to Donald Trump’s militaristic charade, we will host a celebration of what makes America truly great—and truly good.

On June 14, we will gather not just in protest, but in defiance—loud, proud, joyful defiance of a tinpot wannabe tyrant who thinks that celebrating his birthday matters more than honoring the flag that symbolizes our freedom. The Democracy Fair will be an occasion for people to convene after No Kings events being held across the Peninsula.

It will be an active, participatory gathering that includes something for everyone: an exhibit of pro-democracy art, music and theatrical performances on the theme of “No Kings,” tables where people can learn about activism opportunities, a Resistance Lab workshop, a costume competition, and much more.

This event—jointly hosted by Indivisible Mid-Peninsula, Indivisible Palo Alto Plus, and Indivisible Portola Valley, and cosponsored by Bend the Arc, Menlo Park Speaks out, and It’s Blue Turn—will celebrate patriotism, not militarism. *In saying NO to kings, we will also say YES to democracy.*

The Democracy Fair will take place at Rinconada Park, and will follow a parade that starts at 2 p.m. The parade will begin at the intersection of El Camino Real and Embarcadero Road. (We invite participants to join us at any point along the 1.5-mile route.) Please sign up for that event as well. https://www.mobilize.us/nokings/event/792410/

title: Fri. 6/13 > Mass Pike Overpass Standout in Westfield - Southampton Rd (Routes 10/202)
description:
Wow! What a great location for a standout! On 5/30, around 17 people, including a bagpiper!  What a blast! LOTS of engagement with motorists!

There's lots and lots of traffic passing by. Southampton Road (Routes 10/202) is heavily traveled northbound and southbound, and the Mass Pike eastbound and westbound is below. Lots of honks and thumbs up and waves...and a few folks flying middle fingers. We smile and wave at them all! 

We'll have letterboards prepared for the lower part of the overpass fencing - the photo shows how that will look to folks passing on the Mass Pike. We're interacting with motorists on the Mass Pike, and on Southampton Road. We've discovered that the magic happens when we smile and wave to people!

Come when you can, and leave when you must. You needn't be present for the entire 1 1/2 hours.

### How to Get There

The address "130 Southampton Road, Westfield" will get you just north of the overpass. 

### Parking

We can't park in the Southampton Rd breakdown lane. There are vacant business properties north of the bridge, and it seems that parking would be OK there.

It looks like The Wealth Technology Group has vacated their office at 130 Southampton Rd, but the internet says that other businesses are located there, so please be mindful if you decide to park there.

### Etiquette!

We don't give the finger to people who give the finger to us, or who say unpleasant things. We smile and wave to them, too. 

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational in words and body language.

### Other Stuff

Please take everything you brought away with you, and leave the site totally clean.

If rain is predicted, we'll cancel. If we cancel, you'll receive an email notification.

### A Few Requests

We've found that roof rake sections make wonderful flagpoles and banner poles. If you have a roof rake (or 10’-15’ light metal poles or conduit) to contribute, we'll be happy to take it off your hands!

And, if you have an extra 3' x 5' American flag you're not using, we'd love it if you'd pass it on to us!

title: March to the Park!
description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Mark your calendars! Bring the kids! Join us on June 21st @ 10:30am for our March to the Park! from the Tuscarawas Co Courthouse to Tuscora Park (one mile). Join us afterwards for a potluck. Together with the League of Women Voters Tuscarawas County, we are collecting monetary donations for Jack’s House of Hope. 

Departure time: 10:45am! Bring your own signs to this event.

Signs

For this event, please bring your own signs. They can be on wood sticks such as tomatoe posts for ease of carrying. Make your message clear: Federal, state, and local issues of concern to you, your family, the community…there are just so many issues my head would explode if I wrote them all down. Pre-made signs will not be available for this event.

Monetary Donations

Together with the League of Women Voters of Tusc County, we are asking marchers to make a monetary donation of any amount for Jack’s House of Hope. Monetary donations for Jack’s House of Hope will be collected at Tuscora Park. Amanda Fontana, Friends of the Homeless of Tuscarawas County Board of Directors' Secretary will speak about the importance of our local shelter.

March, Eat, Chat, Play!

Our event is from 10:30am-12:30pm. We will march to Tuscora Park from the Tuscarawas County Courthouse and then share a covered dish and/or just bring something for yourself/your family, your own paper products/utensils, snacks to share, and good conversation with those joining us. If you bring something to share, please be mindful of allergies. An index card with a list of ingredients taped to the container would be appreciated. Label containers with your name if you want them back! Jenn Schrock will oversee the food/refreshments while we march.

Half of a covered pavilion near the bocce courts has been reserved for this event. Blankets and chairs can be dropped off beforehand. Marchers can carpool back to the Tusc Co Courthouse to then walk to the park (10:45am). For those that do not have a way back to the courthouse to march, Alicia Hall will help transport people to the courthouse BEFORE the march once they drop off their items at the park.

Remember: Bring your own signs to this event!

Kids can play on the playground equipment. Park rides and Putt-Putt golf open at NOON. See pricing at www.tuscorapark.com/park-info-contact.

We’ll take a group picture!

Helpers

We need helpers at the park to remain with the food, etc. until the marchers arrive. We also need help along the route, guiding marchers as they cross side streets. We don’t block traffic, we hold marchers on the sidewalk while traffic makes their turn left or right onto North Broadway. Let us know if you’re interested in helping.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

title: Cowpokes & Queer Folks Stonewall Anniversary March
description:
First they come is a warning and a battle cry. Texans protect our liberty, our civil rights, our friends and neighbors. 

Join us Saturday, June 28 for a rally and march in honor of Stonewall Anniversary - the riot that launched the queer liberation movement. 

This will be an amazing, creative, loving event with a COWPOKES theme. Drag performances, queer line dancing, crafts, horsies, photo booth, speeches, and a big beautiful march down 4th street!

WHEN: Friday, June 28 from 5 - 9 PM

WHERE: Austin City Hall 

BRING: Your queer family, your regular family, and allll your friends! (Pride flags and American flags welcome!)

PARKING: Please take public transportation and carpool if possible! Parking is available at Austin City Hall ($), Downtown Austin Public Library ($), and Seaholm ($ but Trader J’s has 2 hours free if you use their kiosk and PU a snack). Limited street parking is available around City Hall & across the South 1st ST Bridge at Auditorium Shores (use the Park ATX app with discount codes: FREE15ATX1, FREE15ATX2).

Allies will be out in force to protect Queer Joy. If you are an ally who would like to hold American, Texan, and Queer flags at the event please contact voluteer@handsoffcentraltx.org

Media disclaimer: There will be media and photos/videos of this event taken and shared on the internet, feel free to wear a mask for wellness or privacy reasons, and feel free to take your own photos and videos! Tag us: @handsoffcentraltx #handsofftx #handsoffcentraltx #pridemonth #texaspride #handsofftxqueers

Languages Disclaimer: ASL will not be guaranteed at this event (we are working on fixing this). Language interpretation for languages other than English will not be guaranteed at this event. 

Nonviolent Protest Disclaimer: Nobody from our organization will be provocative and we are not planning civil disobedience. We are utilizing our First Amendment right to protest and our right to lobby our representative government. We do everything in our power to protect the civil rights and physical safety of everyone at our events. We have yet to have any significant incidents of safety issues at any of our events.

By attending our events, you are implicitly agreeing that while you attend our event, you will respect the laws and constitution of the United States and State of Texas and not create or contribute to a safety issue or lawlessness for our attendees and neighbors. We protect our community and defend democracy - we do not put people at risk or threaten violence.

title: NO KINGS Ferrisburgh, Vermont
description:
## Stand Up for Democracy — Join Us for a NO KINGS Rally!

### **NO KINGS** is a national day of action in response to authoritarian excesses and corruption. It’s time to reject a government by billionaires and reclaim a government by the people, for the people.

### We are standing up against corruption, racism, hatred, lies, violence and the threat of authoritarianism.

### We are gathering to support what truly matters: free speech, rule of law, our immigrant neighbors, farmers, small businesses, healthcare workers, researchers, educators, libraries, climate action and so much more! 

### This is a moment to stand together—for justice, for fairness, for the future.

### As part of our event, we’ll cheer on the Relay for Democracy as it passes by. This moving tribute features a U.S. flag that once flew over the US Capitol and was gifted to a World War II veteran who stormed the beaches at Normandy. Carried by Vermonters, the flag will travel the length of Route 7, from Pownal to Highgate, as a symbol of our shared democratic values.

### If you’ve never attended a protest before, now is the time. Many who take that first step find it rewarding, inspiring, energizing, and hopeful. Bring your sign, come by yourself or bring a friend along. You’ll meet like minded people and have fun!

**Democracy needs you. Please stand with us**

#### Carpooling is strongly encouraged. 

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to avoid potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. Avoid engagement and keep a safe distance unless trained for de-escalation. We recommend all participants review the Indivisible safety and security resources before the event.*

title: NO KINGS Leicester, Vermont
description:
## Stand Up for Democracy — Join Us for a NO KINGS Rally!

### **NO KINGS** is a national day of action in response to authoritarian excesses and corruption. It’s time to reject a government by billionaires and reclaim a government by the people, for the people.

### We are standing up against corruption, racism, hatred, lies, violence and the threat of authoritarianism.

### We are gathering to support what truly matters: free speech, rule of law, our immigrant neighbors, farmers, small businesses, healthcare workers, researchers, educators, libraries, climate action and so much more! 

### This is a moment to stand together—for justice, for fairness, for the future.

### As part of our event, we’ll cheer on the Relay for Democracy as it passes by. This moving tribute features a U.S. flag that once flew over the US Capitol and was gifted to a World War II veteran who stormed the beaches at Normandy. Carried by Vermonters, the flag will travel the length of Route 7, from Pownal to Highgate, as a symbol of our shared democratic values.

### If you’ve never attended a protest before, now is the time. Many who take that first step find it rewarding, inspiring, energizing, and hopeful. Bring your sign, come by yourself or bring a friend along. You’ll meet like minded people and have fun!

**Democracy needs you. Please stand with us**

description:
📍 Heritage Station, Huntington, WV

title: Disappeared in America Visual Action
description:
**In America, the government doesn’t get to grab people off the streets, skip the courtroom, and send them straight to a foreign prison.** Disappeared in America is a national day of action to stand up for the rule of law and confront the Trump administration’s illegal abductions, detentions, and deportations of people like Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Rui Marras, and Juan Maldonado Zuniga. 

🚨**On Thursday, June 26th, we’re showing up at courthouses and town squares across the country to say: in America, we don’t let the government disappear people. That’s not who we are.**🚨

Americans believe in rule of law —and the courts are saying that due process is required. If a president can ignore the courts and disappear lawful residents, there is no limit to what can come next. President Trump has said he wants to abduct and deport U.S. citizens. If this isn’t stopped now, no one is safe.

**On June 26th we are launching a national photo petition day where people will take photos with posters of those who have been disappeared and flood social media with the truth.** 

A key focal point of this campaign will be to call on local sheriffs to refuse to cooperate with directives from ICE to engage in federal immigration enforcement, such as renting jail beds to ICE, participating in immigration raids, and transferring people to ICE detentions.  Sheriffs have wide discretion in how much they cooperate with ICE. Participation in federal immigration activities places additional burden on sheriffs’ offices and can erode local community trust in local law enforcement.

_A core principle behind all Disappeared in America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values._

description:

title: Weekly Darrell Issa Office Rallies!
description:
Join us every Friday from 10:30 at Darrell Issa’s Escondido office. We’ll meet first at the office and then walk as a group to the public sidewalk on Lincoln Blvd. Bring your protest signs and a folding chair if you can’t stand for an hour or so. Consider a double-sided sign so that you can have one message for Issa and another for the motorists.

HANDS OFF: Our bodies Our healthcare Our public lands Our education Our human rights

Rallies are a great way to meet other like-minded community members. They remind us that we aren’t alone and it feels good to be civically engaged. Action is the antidote to despair. We guarantee you will feel better about the state of affairs when you leave this event.

Please note that there is a mental health services business in Issa’s office. Please allow a direct path the elevator for patients at all times. Refrain from banging on the glass doors as it has been reported to upset some of the patients. Please follow all posted rules and traffic laws when attending a rally. Safety is always our first priority. Safety patrol volunteers will be wearing bright vests - please comply with their requests at all times.

title: NO KINGS DOWNTOWN TULSA
description:
In America, we don’t bow to kings—and we don’t fight fascism with costume parties.
We fight it by organizing, disrupting, building community, and standing in global solidarity with those resisting oppression.

NO KINGS is a national day of action against Trump’s authoritarian rise and the billionaire-backed movement behind him. He’s attacked our rights, defied the courts, threatened political opponents—and promised to go further. This isn’t about one man’s ego. It’s about confronting the entire system that enables him.

🚨 On Saturday, June 14, we’re not just gathering—we’re showing up with purpose, everywhere he isn’t. 🚨

The flag doesn’t belong to Trump. It belongs to the people. And the people are rising—not just in the U.S., but across the globe.

We don’t ignore it. We name it.
Genocide is happening in Gaza—with U.S. funding and political cover. Resisting fascism here means refusing to be silent about violence abroad. We stand with Palestinians and all people fighting for liberation from empire and occupation.

No crowns. No kings. No fascist future.
Find or organize an action at nokings.org

All No Kings events are rooted in nonviolent action and international solidarity. We don’t perform resistance—we build it, we live it, and we show up across borders, because liberation is collective.

We’re not just showing up to be seen—we’re showing up to serve.

⸻

✨ What to bring:
	•	Water (and extra if you can share!)
	•	Sunblock + a hat
	•	A good mask (N95 or KN95 recommended)
	•	A charged phone (turn off face/fingerprint ID)
	•	Emergency/legal support number written on your body
	•	Snacks + anything you need to stay safe and comfortable in the heat

⸻

🛍️ Donations Needed!

We’ll be feeding and supporting our unhoused neighbors during this action. Mutual aid is resistance.

If you can, please bring:
	•	New socks
	•	Travel-size hygiene supplies (individually packed)
	•	Wet wipes
	•	Easy-to-eat snacks (soft granola bars, fruit pouches, applesauce)
	•	Electrolyte drinks or Gatorade

👉 Specific donation asks will be posted soon—stay tuned!

⸻

🔒 Security Culture Reminders:
	•	No livestreaming
	•	Cover identifying tattoos and facial features if needed
	•	Always ask for consent before taking photos or videos
	•	No weapons, alcohol, drugs, or illegal items

⸻

We keep us safe. We show up for each other. We resist with care—and we do it together.

title: No Kings- No Time to Celebrate
description:
On Flag Day Saturday June 14th, stand with us on the sidewalk at the corner of Maple Street and Lafayette Street (Route 114) in Marblehead from 5 p.m. to 6 p.m., for “No Kings- No Time to Celebrate” —a nonpartisan, peaceful stand out to stand up in defense of American democracy.

This is no time to celebrate. America is in a Constitutional crisis. 

The colors of the American flag have been described as “Red for courage and readiness to sacrifice; white for pure intentions and high ideals; and blue for vigilance and justice.” Our Veterans have fought and died to defend our flag and our values and we should not betray their sacrifice. 
On this Flag Day in 2025, we call on those same qualities of American spirit- courage and sacrifice, vigilance and justice- as we defend the pillars of democracy.  We refuse to celebrate when America is in a Constitutional crisis.

Come to this peaceful demonstration. Bring your signs, your friends, your determination—and your belief that the United States was never meant to have kings. Join us!

Organized by the Marblehead Alliance for Democracy.

title: GOOD TROUBLE LIVES ON: Williamsburg, VA
description:
ALL OUR ACTIONS WILL BE PEACEFUL, RESPECTFUL and SAFE!!!

Our rights are under attack. Our democracy is under siege. We’ve been here before, and we know what to do.

On July 17, we honor the anniversary of the passing of civil rights hero John Lewis, not with ceremonies, but with action. Across the country, we will take to the streets, courthouses, and community spaces to carry forward his fight for justice, voting rights, and dignity for all.

This is more than a protest, it’s a moral reckoning. A continuation of the movement Lewis helped lead, and a new front in the struggle for freedom.

**Please note:** a core principle behind our John Lewis Good Trouble Day actions is a commitment to nonviolence in all we do. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

This is more than a protest, it’s a moral reckoning. A continuation of the movement Lewis helped lead, and a new front in the struggle for freedom.

COMMUNITY NORMS:

Please read before attending one of our events.

One of our main objectives is to host PEACEFUL, RESPECTFUL and SAFE EVENTS. Remember, when attending a Williamsburg JCC Indivisible event, your actions represent our group, and you are expected to conform to the Community Norms. Safety is a top priority for our attendees. We wish to remind everyone that we do not react to those drivers who make it clear they do not support us by aggravating them through screaming obscenities or making certain hand gestures. We do not want to enrage them and potentially make everyone, including other drivers, less safe. It is easier to wave at everyone and say, “Have a nice day”.

At our events, please do not hold signs or otherwise promote other events that Williamsburg JCC Indivisible is not hosting. You may be placing a potential legal liability onto our group that we are NOT willing to accept.

Please do not engage in DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOURS! If you are asked to stop engaging in activities which are disrupting an event to the point people are complaining to the hosts that they are experiencing physical or emotional trauma, it is expected that you will be respectful of others and follow our Community Norms and stop those behaviours. Loud noises, such as, but not limited to, cowbells, horns, etc., are usually deployed by counter-protesters to disrupt an event, not by attendees participating in an event. If you refuse to disengage from such thoughtless behaviours, do not ruin the event for everyone else - please be kind and leave!

As with our previous events, the same rules apply. We will not engage with counter-protesters. If an issue arises, please notify one of the event organizers. At larger events, these organizers will be wearing Williamsburg JCC Indivisible T-shirts with yellow safety vests. We will not engage in any acts of violence or violation of any applicable laws or engage in civil disobedience. All actions will be peaceful. Everyone participating in this event will be required to behave lawfully to ensure the safety of event participants and will seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. We will obey the orders of authorized event marshals and law enforcement authorities. Event organizers will not be responsible for any injury or damage if any were to occur during this event. Each individual is responsible for the consequences of their actions and attends at their own risk. We will park in the Courthouse parking lot without blocking access lanes and will remove any trash that is left. We are committed to maintaining public health measures to practice safe protesting during these times. Please wear a mask and socially distance if that makes you more comfortable - weigh your own risk in attending. Follow all local safety guidelines at minimum, and any safety instructions from hosts that exceed local law.

title: Overpass Rally Boxford
description:
This Juneteenth, join us in a visible, peaceful demonstration to honor the fight for Black freedom—and to demand accountability from those in power today.

As we commemorate the end of slavery, we also confront a system that still concentrates wealth and power in the hands of the few. Our message is clear:

No Kings — We reject authoritarianism, elite rule, and leaders who place themselves above the people.

No Blank Checks — We demand transparency and responsibility in how our government spends public money. This budget bill shows where their priorities lie—billions for war and surveillance, while our communities are left behind.

While they pour funds into power and control, our schools, housing, healthcare, and future go underfunded. We're here to say: our tax dollars should serve the people, not the powerful.

Bring your signs, your friends, and your voice. Stand on the overpass with us and be part of the message.

title: Indivisible Douglas County - Summer of Solidarity Saturdays

description:
# Let's Make Our Voices Heard!

**Indivisible Douglas County** invites you to join us every Saturday this summer in solidarity and protest against the Trump administration. We are coming together on a weekly basis to show Douglas County, the state of Oregon, the country, and the world that we will not will not stand for tyranny. 

**Join us!** Bring your creative protest signs, your voice, your spirit, and your family and friends along with you. Let's show our community that we are not okay with what is happening in this country, and we have something to say about it! Be vocal, have fun, and keep it peaceful.

Our plan is to protest along the sidewalks of Garden Valley Blvd in Roseburg from in front of the BLM building's green space, in both directions. 

This a local Indivisible event!

title: Avelo Airline Nationwide Protest
description:
**Indivisible Mesa is joining the Coalition to Stop Avelo's nationwide call to action for a full boycott of Avelo Airlines and organizing protests at all 54 airports where they operate.** Our goal? Drive ticket sales to ZERO and make Avelo feel the consequences of profiting from deportations.

On May 31st, Indivisible Mesa was part of the **26 protests across the country** who came together to protest Avelo Airlines on the same day for the first time! To keep the pressure on Avelo, the Coalition is planning to support additional nationwide protests and Indivisible Mesa is again joining the call!!

**Indivisible Mesa will be protesting against Avelo Airlines operating ICE deportations on Saturday, June 28th!** 

By protesting together, everywhere, on the same day, we elevate our anti-Avelo movement from a local news story to a can't miss national news story!

🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨

The message to **Avelo** is simple: **"Cancel your contract with ICE."**

The message to **City Hall** is simple: **"Stop funding Avelo with local dollars."**

The message to **travelers** is simple: **"Boycott Avelo, don't give them your money."**

The message to **allies** is simple: **"Join us. Stand for justice. Fight inhumanity."**

And the message to the **world** is powerful: 
*We stand for families. 
We stand for immigration rights. 
We stand for due process. 
We stand for all Americans who are feeling scared and vulnerable. 
We stand against companies that sacrifice people for profit. 
We stand against blood money and we stand against deals-with-the-devil. We stand against Avelo's contract with ICE. 
And we stand together, together, together. 
We will win this fight! 
We will force Avelo to cancel its ICE contract.**

Protest locally, speak nationally.

✨Be safe, be lawful, be loud. Bring signs. Bring friends. Take pics.✨


==**Protest Information**==

🌄 Indivisible Mesa will be at the intersection of East Ray Rd and Power Rd.

🅿️ There is PLENTY of parking in the store surrounding the intersection, including Walmart, Target, etc. 

❄️Bring all the things to keep yourself cool like cooling towels, umbrellas for shade, water, etc. and feel free to bring extra for other protestors if you are able to!

🔥Indivisible Mesa leadership realizes it may be too hot for some to attend the event, but we have to be outside and as visible as possible. IT'S VITAL. **If this means you can only protest for 20 mins, then please come for 20 mins!! Everybody and every minute counts!!**


==**Signs & Graphics**==
Please create signs and graphics that are relevant to Avelo & Mesa Gateway Airport! The messaging we put on our signs can do a lot to cut right through Mesa Gateway's bureaucratic smokescreen. 

   ☑️ Call attention to Avelo Airlines separating families

   ☑️ Complicity of Mesa/Gateway airport

   ☑️ Illegal deportations without due process

   ☑️ Human trafficking

   ☑️ Rather overheat than let human trafficking continue

   ☑️ Print out large pics of ICE kidnapping people in Phoenix

Please share and bring friends to protest against these flights that are illegal, inhumane, & unconstitutional.

title: No Kings, Let Freedom Fly
description:
Let Freedom Fly! in downtown Brattleboro on Flag Day from 3-6 pm. On Saturday, June 14, we’ll again join others nationwide, standing together in love and unity. Our movement for justice continues to build: We declare that power belongs with the people. That’s US! That’s each and every one of YOU!

Come out and make noise with us in Brattleboro!  We’ll gather at Centre Congregational Church at 3:00 pm, 193 Main, parade with The Peoples Resistance Marching Band and The Good Trouble Street Choir to the Common.  Local groups will table for information-sharing and grassroots strength-building.  We'll hear briefly from a few speakers and enjoy strolling musicians and other entertainment. Food trucks include Cocina Lupita, Jamaican Jewelz and Crossroads! 

We will celebrate the diversity that makes America shine: bring your favorite flags–country, pride, issue or anything that shows who you are and what you love!

*We honor the flag of the United States, a symbol of freedom and national solidarity. Together we demand that OUR Constitution be upheld, that the government respect the rule of law including the rights of every person within these borders.

As Martin Luther King Jr. said, “A time comes when silence is betrayal.”  We will not be silent, we will gather on the streets on June 14 and in our neighborhoods in collaboration, every day to follow.  
“The work of bringing people together in mutual recognition and cooperation is never really done”.  –Archbishop Anthony Broglio

For more info, email DiverseUSA@proton.me

*This is intended as a family-friendly, safe, and peaceful protest.

We are committed to complying fully with all town requests and guidelines, including:

    Remaining on the sidewalk at all times
    Following all traffic lights and pedestrian signals
    Respecting public safety personnel and instructions

This event is intended to be welcoming for all ages, inclusive, and non-disruptive. We believe in exercising our First Amendment rights with respect and responsibility, and we thank the community and local officials for their support in making this a safe gathering for everyone.

Let’s show up in solidarity and peace.

Co-hosted by Brattleboro Area Action and Indivisible Brattleboro, this partnership is bound by a shared commitment to nonviolence, inclusion, and democratic participation.

description: If you cannot make it to Topeka, we are holding one here in Salina. It is scheduled to coincide with the President's $40 million birthday military parade in Washington DC, in order to draw attention away from this event, and rather to model, for local communities like Ephraim, alternatives to the administration's prioritization of billionaires over working Americans, its displays of militarism, increased authoritarianism, and other violations of basic civil/constitutional rights and public trust. (Although the No Kings event responds most specifically to these concerns with the Trump administration, participants are welcome to voice/represent any other such concerns they may have, extending beyond partisan lines.)

Bring an American flag, bring your sign, come walk with fellow Sanpeters!



**In the US, we don’t trifle with would-be kings.**

title: NO KINGS! We're Taking Over the Streets of East Portland!

description:

🚫👑 No thrones. 🇺🇸 No crowns. 🇺🇸 No kings. 
And no more Donald Trump trying to rule like one.

## We’re filling a square mile of Portland’s east side sidewalks with protest, purpose, and people power!  🗽🪇🥁                                 
From the Convention Center to Broadway, from MLK to Grand, Saturday morning, June 14th, we’re taking over the sidewalks in one loud, united voice. 

**NO KINGS is a national day of action and mass mobilization in response to increasing authoritarian excesses and corruption from Trump and his allies.** We’ve watched as they’ve cracked down on free speech, detained people for their political views, threatened to deport American citizens, and defied the courts. They’ve done this all while continuing to serve and enrich their billionaire allies.

🚨**On Saturday, June 14, we’re taking to the streets nationwide. We’re not gathering to feed his ego. We’re building a movement that leaves him behind.**🚨

💪 We’re standing together with friends, neighbors, allies, and special guests;💪 Building Solidarity! We all know what’s at stake. We need everyone's energy and action! 💪


 **Bring your flags. 🏳️‍🌈🏳️‍⚧️ 🇺🇸 Bring your signs. Bring your bells and noisemakers. 🎺🥁Bring your people. Let us know if you have a band, theater troup, 🎭 kazoo chorus, community organization or 🎨 artist group and you'd like to put on something special.**🎭  districtoneneighbors@gmail.com 

#### Now through June 14th, 🚨 Here's how you can help get out the word about No Kings Day ####

* Join or Host a Pop Up Protest  https://www.mobilize.us/oepindivisible/event/796793/

accessibility_notes:
What are we fighting for? 

	No kings is a national call to action and mass mobilization in response to the increasing authoritarian excesses and corruption of the Trump administration. Trump is planning a military parade in Washington D.C. on June 14th. This display of his is intended to intimidate political opponents and solidify his image as “king” and he is paying for it with our tax dollars. We are taking action everywhere in America that isn't D.C. to take the attention away from Trump and put it on us, the people of the United States. We the people do not condone using important tax dollars for Trump to throw himself a birthday party. We do not support Trump using the military as a pawn in his political game. We stand united against kings since 1776 to today. 


What do we bring?

	The goal is to be comfortable for the one hour we plan to be demonstrating. Please use your best judgement on what would be appropriate for this peaceful event. Some ideas of what could make it on your packing list to bring:  a friend, your family, a sign that shows why you are attending(slogan ideas to follow), a water source, a lawn chair.

Where should we park?
	
	Please use public parking along Main street and Buffalo street. If you know anyone in the neighborhood, you could ask to park at their house. If you are physically able, consider walking. 

Where are we meeting?
	
	We will congregate in front of the Marion Town Hall and will populate the corner of Main Street/Buffalo Street. We will not block any streets or sidewalks. All roadways and walkways will remain accessible and open. No businesses will be blocked including any buildings we may find ourselves in front of. Please be mindful of making room for others using the public space who are not a part of this demonstration. 

What do we do when we get there?

	Event Organizers will make an introduction and speak on behalf of the cause. Among the group we encourage you to share your story, share with others why you're here or why this is important to you or for the town of Marion. We aren't gathering just to stand against oligarchy, we are building community and that takes vulnerability. If you feel awkward or embarrassed, please know you're not the only one! Showing up takes guts and humility. Being afraid is the first step to being brave and your courage will not go unnoticed by your community! We are stronger together. 

Following the protest we encourage you to shop Main street, visit the park or cemetery or stop into the Marion Public Library prior to our demonstration. Enjoy what Marion has to offer,  we want to make a statement of investing into our community!

What if this event escalates negatively? 

	Our event organizers will participate in training that will help them mitigate any negative incidents. The most important thing to remember is that you cannot control anyone's actions but your own. Remain peaceful, do not engage with counter-protesters, and follow the directions and leadership of event organizers. 

	Interested protesters can attend a Know Your Rights Training hosted by the ACLU. This online training is open to the public and will happen on June 10th at 7 pm.  Use this Link or copy this web address into your web browser to register. 

https://act.aclu.org/a/2025-kyr-training-2?/utm_source=email&source=nokingshostemail

What should I write on my sign?
	
No Kings Since 1776
Marion says No Kings!
The People United Can Never be Defeated
Oligarchy (with an X through the word) 
Money for Medicaid not Parades
For Democracy! No Kings.
Liberty and Justice for ALL

There should be nothing vulgar and no offensive language, please always defer to our base rules of peace and respect. No insults, slurs, bad jokes, or any other negative leaning statement or image.

title: Lemon Sticks with Lawmakers
description:
🍋 Lemon Sticks with a Lawmaker 🍋
Presented by Indivisible Baltimore County at Sounds of Solidarity
June 21 | 11AM–4PM | Patterson Park, Baltimore City

Come cool off with a sweet Baltimore tradition- and a little political zest.

Join us for Lemon Sticks with a Lawmaker, where constituents and elected officials meet face-to-face in the heart of the park. It’s a chance to share the sweet and the sour- because real dialogue is how we get through the tough stuff together.

In sour times, sweeten it up with real talk and real connections- solidarity is our secret ingredient.

Bring your questions, your hopes, and your appetite for change.
🎶 Music, community, and citrus-powered conversation await!

* timing for elected officials' arrival will be dependent on individual schedules *

Thinking about running for office? Indivisible Baltimore County supports a bottom-up approach to making real change in our communities. Indivisible is a progressive movement- while we do not endorse candidates, we do endorse conversations, and this is the perfect place to make yourself heard!

For more information on Indivisible Baltimore County, visit: https://indivisible-baltimorecounty.org



More on Sounds of Solidarity:

The Free State Coalition is thrilled to invite you to be a part of the SOUNDS OF SOLIDARITY, FETE DE LA MUSIQUE, a one day celebration of International Music Day that highlights community, and collective action in support of democracy for all. This event will take place on June 21 at Patterson Park. 

The Sound of Solidarity Festival aims to:

Celebrate International Music Day by showcasing the power of music to inspire change.

Provide a platform for artists whose music promotes freedom, resistance, and joy.

Raise awareness and support for social justice causes through partnerships with non-profit organizations.

Create an inclusive community event that celebrates diversity and promotes solidarity.

Support local artists, vendors, and businesses.

We envision Sound of Solidarity- Fete de la Musique to be a powerful demonstration of what we can achieve when we come together in the spirit of solidarity. We hope you will join us in making this event a success.

title: NO KINGS!!   Flag Day Celebration in Heber

location.venue: Sidewalk in front of the County Building and Heber City Hall

description:

Let's send our message - our country has NO KING! Folks of all ages are welcome to join this "Flag Day" March. Dress colorfully and bring American flags and small musical instruments if you wish. Uncle Sam will be joining us! We plan to have bagpipes and drums playing as we march. Bring signs expressing your views - but no vulgar language please, as this is meant to be family-friendly. title: Disappeared in America Visual Action
description:
**In America, the government doesn’t get to grab people off the streets, skip the courtroom, and send them straight to a foreign prison.** Disappeared in America is a national day of action to stand up for the rule of law and confront the Trump administration’s illegal abductions, detentions, and deportations of people like Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Rui Marras, and Juan Maldonado Zuniga. 

🚨**On Thursday, June 26th, we’re showing up at courthouses and town squares across the country to say: in America, we don’t let the government disappear people. That’s not who we are.**🚨

Americans believe in rule of law —and the courts are saying that due process is required. If a president can ignore the courts and disappear lawful residents, there is no limit to what can come next. President Trump has said he wants to abduct and deport U.S. citizens. If this isn’t stopped now, no one is safe.

**On June 26th we are launching a national photo petition day where people will take photos with posters of those who have been disappeared and flood social media with the truth.** 

A key focal point of this campaign will be to call on local sheriffs to refuse to cooperate with directives from ICE to engage in federal immigration enforcement, such as renting jail beds to ICE, participating in immigration raids, and transferring people to ICE detentions.  Sheriffs have wide discretion in how much they cooperate with ICE. Participation in federal immigration activities places additional burden on sheriffs’ offices and can erode local community trust in local law enforcement.

_A core principle behind all Disappeared in America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values._

title: Resist Tyranny Bridge Brigade

location.venue: Old Riverhead Road, Westhampton Beach, NY 11978

description:
Join the Resist Tyranny Bridge Brigade

This Independence Day weekend, as families head east to enjoy the beauty of Long Island, let’s come together to remind them what this holiday is truly about: freedom, independence, and the power of the people.

The Declaration of Independence tells us that all people are born with the rights to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. And when a government fails to protect those rights, the people have the power—and the responsibility—to demand change.

Let’s proudly show that Long Islanders celebrate democracy, freedom, and the spirit of resistance. Bring your flags, signs, and energy. Let’s line the overpasses and make it clear: we are a people who believe in liberty and justice for all.

Resist Tyranny. Defend Democracy. Stand Together. 

Organized by Indivisible Long Island 
Follow us on BlueSky - @indivisibleli.bsky.social‬
Email - IndivisibleLI2025@gmail.com 

We are a 100% volunteer group, please consider supporting our ongoing efforts by making a donation here:

description:

No thrones. No crowns. No kings. And no more Donald Trump trying to rule like one.

We’re filling a full square mile of Portland’s east side sidewalks with protest, purpose, and people power.

From the Convention Center to Broadway, from MLK to Grand, we’re taking over the sidewalks in one loud, united voice.

NO KINGS is a national day of action and mass mobilization in response to increasing authoritarian excesses and corruption from Trump and his allies. 🎨 Bring your flags. Bring your signs. Bring your bells and noisemakers. Bring your people. Let us know if you have a band, theater, or art group and you'd like to put on something special.🎭 districtoneneighbors@gmail.com

Now through June 14th, help get out the word about No Kings Day

title: A Funeral for the Constitution - A Peaceful Protest of the Inaction of Senator Thom Tillis
description:
Join us on August 23, we will gather in downtown Greensboro dressed in black, not in celebration - but in mourning.
This solemn protest, led by concerned citizens across North Carolina, is a funeral march for our Constitution - the foundational document Senator Thom Tillis continues to undermine and nullify, piece by piece.
As we carry a symbolic coffin through the streets, accompanied by the haunting sound of a lone bagpipe, we will grieve the erosion of civil liberties, voting rights, and democratic norms. This is not a spectacle. This is a eulogy - for fairness, for accountability, and for a government of the people.

With peaceful resolve and powerful symbolism, we will honor what has been lost and demand better from those elected to serve us. We mourn, we march, and we resist - because democracy should not die in silence.

title: Get in Line, Senator Tillis
description:
This joyful protest gets in step for justice - literally.
"Joy is a form of resistance" is often attributed to the poet Toi Derricotte.

We're dancing to send a clear and unified message to Senator Thom Tillis: it's time to GET IN LINE with the people of North Carolina! While he continues to ignore the will of his constituents, we're responding not with silence, but with rhythm, joy and movement! Our feet will hit the ground in Guilford County on July 12, where every step is a stand - a stand for community building, for kindness, and for those whose voices have been sidelined.

With music, unity and purpose, we're turning this protest into a celebration and resistance into motion! Join us - because when we move together, we shift the future, and we won't stop dancing until our representatives fall in line with the people they serve!

title: Protest @ Tesla Lyndhurst, Thursday, June 12th, 12:00 to 2:00 PM
description:
Musk Quit - We Won't!

Okay, Musk and Trump had a falling out.  That's no surprise.  Everyone who kowtows to Trump eventually finds out that he turns against them.  Should we feel sorry for Musk?  NO!  He paid $270M to get Trump elected which makes him responsible for the madness that is now going on in our country.  Should we stop protesting at Tesla?  NO.  The damage that he has done with DOGE will impact us for years to come and we need to remind Musk how we feel about that.  So come to the Tesla store and send a message to Musk and show other politicians how "We, The People" stand up to protect our democracy against people like him.  And know that we are having an impact!

Rules & Reminders: Bring a sign. Stay on the sidewalk & allow pedestrians to pass. Do not jaywalk across Mayfield Road (police will be watching). Use the crosswalk just west of Tesla. Don't block driveway entrances or exits. Don't harass Tesla customers or employees. Do not argue with counter protesters - especially those driving vehicles. Do not use inflammatory language or make threats. Watch for peacekeepers in yellow vests and immediately report any disturbances to them. Follow any instructions from Lyndhurst Police. PROTEST PEACEFULLY.

Parking is available at Messiah Lutheran Church, 5200 Mayfield Road. Please be respectful and park on the EAST SIDE of the lot first (away from the Tesla Store). Additional parking is available at the Lyndhurst Community of Faith Church, 5312 Mayfield Road. Please enter the EAST DRIVEWAY as the west driveway is exit only.

title: March with NY WFP at Brooklyn Pride!
description:
It's Pride!! As LGBTQIA+ Communities are under attack across the country, Brooklyn Pride is an opportunity to celebrate our communities, to show up, and to build community for city leadership that reflects our city and our communities' values.

Join the New York Working Families Party on Saturday, June 14, following the first day of Early Voting in the New York City Primary Election, as we march with our elected allies and talk to voters about the key elections for City Council, for Mayor, and for other citywide offices.

In order to BLOCK Andrew Cuomo and elect a mayor who will prioritize the needs of working families above the demands of the rich and well-connected, we need ALL HANDS ON DECK to remind voters to #RankTheSlate: #1 Zohran Mamdani, #2 Brad Lander, #3 Adrienne Adams, and #4 Zellnor Myrie. Because we need candidates for EVERY office fighting for working people, we’re also encouraging voters to vote for Justin Brannan for Comptroller and Jumaane Williams for Public Advocate—two progressive champions who are committed to fighting for working families, as well as Council Member Shahana Hanif's re-election campaign.

WHEN: 6:30 PM.
WHERE: Lincoln Place and Fifth Avenue in Park Slope. (RSVP for meet-up location updates).

NY Working Families Party members will also be present throughout the day at the Brooklyn Pride Festival, which begins at 11:00 AM, to talk with voters, as well as at pollsites across the city. 

Sign-up for a pollsite shift: http://wfpus.org/nycearlyvoting
If you will be at Brooklyn Pride earlier and would like to support, please email: keanuarpelsjosiah@gmail.com.

title: FCTC Community Listening Session

location.venue: Orange Mound Library - Memphis Public Libraries

description: From Court to Classroom: Shifting the Truancy Narrative is a passion-led, two-phase campaign designed to build both understanding and support systems for students experiencing chronic absenteeism or truancy. We would like to invite you to phase 1 of the campaign. Phase 1 will focus on hosting a community listening session with 8–10 youth-centered organizations in Memphis to explore the social and structural barriers that contribute to school absenteeism. Insights from these conversations will be synthesized alongside state-level data to draft a community-informed "truancy toolkit." This phase will also include inviting organizations to collaboratively propose a citywide intervention to address truancy.

title: Elbows Up - Buffalo
description:
International Day of Action in Solidarity with Canada—Good Neighbors Getting It Done and Power to the People Western New York, will peacefully rally concerned members of the community to say, “We oppose President Trump's tariffs and threats to annex Canada as the 51st state. We vehemently oppose creating a false emergency on the border as a pretext to invoke the Insurrection Act.”

A coalition of Indivisible and allied groups from Skagway, Alaska to Burlington, VT (to London, UK!) will line the longest undefended border in the world to stand in solidarity and friendship with our Canadian allies and neighbors.

Canada is its own sovereign nation, and has long been one of America’s closest allies, repeatedly giving aid—from September 11th to the recent California fires, among countless examples. Canadians came to help. Canada deserves more than Donald Trump’s lies. Every day that these tariffs are in place, it will cost families, communities, and businesses on both sides of our long border. They will increase the cost of just about everything for all of us. Border communities benefit immensely from our partnerships with one another. We have each other’s backs. The damage done to the relationship and the economy of border communities is palpable. The trust violated, profound.
 
We will rally at Bufffalo’s Freedom Park on the American side of the Niagara River, and line up along the Bird Island Pier to wave to our Canadian friends in the Freedom Park in Fort Erie, Ontario.

title: No Kings/Kick Out the Clowns
description:
On June 14, our clown-king will honor himself with a four-mile military parade in our nation’s capitol. This tacky parade will cost taxpayers millions of dollars. Join us in protest of this ridiculous example of government waste.

WHEN: Saturday, June 14 from 5 - 8 PM

WHERE: TX Capitol Front Steps

BRING: EVERYONE. Bring your family and friends and your creative protest signs (No sticks longer than 12 inches are allowed by Capitol DPS including flag poles.)

Our grassroots street circus will turn satire into resistance and reclaim the big tent for democracy.

Women’s March KICK OUT THE CLOWNS: When you elect clowns, the country becomes a circus. 🤡 This will be a day of bold, creative actions in protest of the chaos that has been sown across the country. Together, we’ll set a national record for the most circuses held in a single day while we simultaneously refuse to celebrate a petty clown who desperately wants to be seen as strong. We won’t stop until we build the country we all deserve.

Indivisible’s NO KINGS is a national day of action and mass mobilization in response to increasing authoritarian excesses and corruption. The flag doesn’t belong to those that seek to destroy our country - it belongs to us. Join us to make history.

MOBILITY: We will be marching around the TX Capitol, not outside of Capitol grounds. If you have mobility concerns, you are welcome to stand firm at the front steps of the TX Capitol. Capitol bathrooms are ADA accessible.

DEETS: Bathrooms are available inside the Capitol. You will have to pass through a DPS security checkpoint to access bathrooms. Emergency water will be available on-site but please bring your own.

TRANSPORTATION & PARKING: CAPMETRO bus lines 1, 10, 103, 20, and 3 drop off near the Capitol, plan your trip. Please park at the Capitol Visitors Parking Garage (free for the first 2 hours), or park on the street in the neighborhoods west of the TX Capitol using the Park ATX app with discount codes: FREE15ATX1, FREE15ATX2

KEEP IN MIND: Soliciting donations and selling products is not allowed on Capitol grounds. We respect the DPS rules so that we can continue to have impactful mass mobilization efforts on OUR Capitol grounds!

SAFETY: We have a team of volunteers, legal observers, and street medics coming to this event. If you would like to volunteer for any of these teams, please use this form to contact us!

Veteran? We have a veterans arm of Hands Off Central TX. Plug in on-site to defend democracy, the constitution, and our first amendment rights. Email your interest to veterans@handsoffcentraltx.org

If your organization would like to partner with us to defend democracy, please email our lead wrangler (AKA Board President) president@handsoffcentraltx.org

Media disclaimer: There will be media and photos/videos of this event taken and shared on the internet, feel free to wear a mask for wellness or privacy reasons, and feel free to take your own photos and videos! Tag us: @handsoffcentraltx #handsofftx #nokings #kickouttheclown

Languages Disclaimer: ASL will be available for all speakers. Language interpretation for languages other than English will not be guaranteed at this event. 

Nonviolent Protest Disclaimer: Nobody from our organization will be provocative and we are not planning civil disobedience. We are utilizing our First Amendment right to protest and our right to lobby our representative government. We do everything in our power to protect the civil rights and physical safety of everyone at our events. We have yet to have any significant incidents of safety issues at any of our events.

By attending our events, you are implicitly agreeing that while you attend our event, you will respect the laws and constitution of the United States and State of Texas and not create or contribute to a safety issue or lawlessness for our attendees and neighbors. We protect our community and defend democracy - we do not put people at risk or threaten violence.

description:

title: Disappeared in America Visual Action
description:
**In America, the government doesn’t get to grab people off the streets, skip the courtroom, and send them straight to a foreign prison.** 

Disappeared in America is a national day of action to stand up for the rule of law and confront the Trump administration’s illegal abductions, detentions, and deportations of people like Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Rui Marras, and Juan Maldonado Zuniga. 

🚨**On Thursday, June 26th, we’re showing up at courthouses and town squares across the country to say: extrajudicial kidnappings have no place in our country. The USA is a nation founded on free speech, due process, and liberty. We will gather to demand the end of extrajudicial kidnappings by ICE and the Trump administration.**🚨

Americans believe in rule of law —and the courts are saying that due process is required. If a president can ignore the courts and disappear lawful residents, there is no limit to what can come next. President Trump has said he wants to abduct and deport U.S. citizens. If this isn’t stopped now, no one is safe.

**On June 26th we are launching a national photo petition day where people will take photos with posters of those who have been disappeared and flood social media with the truth.** 

A key focal point of this campaign will be to call on local sheriffs to refuse to cooperate with directives from ICE to engage in federal immigration enforcement, such as renting jail beds to ICE, participating in immigration raids, and transferring people to ICE detentions.  Sheriffs have wide discretion in how much they cooperate with ICE. Participation in federal immigration activities places additional burden on sheriffs’ offices and can erode local community trust in local law enforcement.

_A core principle behind all Disappeared in America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values._
accessibility_notes: Primary location is the sidewalk in front of the large federal courthouse building. No onsite parking is available; no public restrooms are available.

title: #TeslaTakedown Santa Monica
description:
Elon Musk is destroying our democracy, and he's using the fortune he built at Tesla to do it. We are taking action at Tesla to stop Musk's illegal coup.

⚡ We're tanking Tesla's stock price to stop Musk.

Elon Musk has, of course, earned his popular association with such ugly symbols, but we risk being misconstrued or offending potential allies by having them all over our signs. Again, winning as many hearts and minds as possible is our aim.

title: Disappeared in America Visual Action
description:
**In America, the government doesn’t get to grab people off the streets, skip the courtroom, and send them straight to a foreign prison.** Disappeared in America is a national day of action to stand up for the rule of law and confront the Trump administration’s illegal abductions, detentions, and deportations of people like Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Rui Marras, and Juan Maldonado Zuniga. 

🚨**On Thursday, June 26th, we’re showing up at courthouses and town squares across the country to say: in America, we don’t let the government disappear people. That’s not who we are.**🚨

Americans believe in rule of law —and the courts are saying that due process is required. If a president can ignore the courts and disappear lawful residents, there is no limit to what can come next. President Trump has said he wants to abduct and deport U.S. citizens. If this isn’t stopped now, no one is safe.

**On June 26th we are launching a national photo petition day where people will take photos with posters of those who have been disappeared and flood social media with the truth.** 

A key focal point of this campaign will be to call on local sheriffs to refuse to cooperate with directives from ICE to engage in federal immigration enforcement, such as renting jail beds to ICE, participating in immigration raids, and transferring people to ICE detentions.  Sheriffs have wide discretion in how much they cooperate with ICE. Participation in federal immigration activities places additional burden on sheriffs’ offices and can erode local community trust in local law enforcement.

_A core principle behind all Disappeared in America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values._

title: Franklin Township, NJ: Rally to Stop The NESE Pipeline
description:
The NESE pipeline is BACK. **Trump wants to fast-track this dangerous polluting project here in Central Jersey — and we need your help to stop it again!**

On Thursday evening, the Franklin Township Council will consider a resolution opposing NESE once again. Join us to rally at 6 p.m. in front of the Franklin Municipal Complex (at the gazebo) ahead of the meeting to show strong opposition to this zombie project.

Municipal resolutions send a powerful message to the Governor and other decision-makers and are an effective way to push for change at the local level. **Join us to speak out against this un-NESE-sary pipeline!**


### About NESE:

The Northeast Supply Enhancement (NESE) proposal calls for construction of a gas-powered gas compressor station in Franklin Township, as well as 3.5 miles of connecting pipeline through Old Bridge and 23 miles of new pipeline under the Raritan Bay / New York Harbor.

NESE would pollute our water, increase flooding, destroy critical wetlands and habitats, and would cut through the already-polluted and sensitive Raritan Bay and New York Bay. Pipelines leak enormous amounts of methane, a stronger greenhouse gas than CO2, which directly contributes to climate change.

The proposed compressor station in Franklin would release air- and water-polluting toxins. The gases emitted by a compressor station can increase the risk of asthma as well as cardiovascular, neurological, developmental, and respiratory diseases.

This project is not in the public interest for New Jersey residents. Our communities in New Jersey will receive the direct impacts of pipeline leakage and compressor station pollution, while none of the gas is even for New Jersey.

**We defeated NESE last year, and we can do it again. Join us as we get organized and rally against zombie NESE!**

title: NO NUKES VIGIL - Every Friday
description: The Santa Fe chapter of Veterans For Peace started this vigil in 2002 and have continued it every Friday at noon for 23 years. Its purpose is to bring awareness to the hundreds of billions of our tax dollars going to the production of new nuclear weapons here in our state. Many people, even many New Mexicans, are unaware that Los Alamos National Lab is currently building several new bomb factories to increase production of nuclear bomb cores (known as plutonium "pits") to reach a goal of 30 to 120 new pits per year. Each pit, on average, has the destructive power of 20 Hiroshima-sized bombs. Loud public outcry may be able to halt this waste of federal money, or at least slow it down until we elect a saner administration. Life on Earth is at stake.

title: No Kings Nationwide Day of Defiance
description:
This event was formerly the Indivisible Oregon 2nd Saturday event, and was changed to direct people to the NO KINGS Day of Defiance.  Please find a NO KINGS event to attend or join us with other local Indivisible groups at Salmon Street Springs.

On June 14th—Flag Day—Trump is staging a $50 million military parade in D.C., complete with tanks, warplanes, and thousands of troops. While MAGA shows off raw power, they’re slashing Medicaid, food assistance, and other life-saving services. It’s a spectacle meant to intimidate—but we won’t be silent.

Join local Indivisible groups in Portland for NO KINGS—a national day of defiance against authoritarianism and far-right extremism.

We’ll rally at Salmon St Springs at Portland’s waterfront with music, performers, and powerful voices. From civil rights to antiwar movements, music has always fueled resistance and brought communities together in protest. After the rally, we’ll take that spirit and join the marchers as they leave the waterfront.

This is a peaceful, nonviolent protest—one rooted in hope, solidarity, and the power of collective action.

NO KINGS IN AMERICA.

title: Mondays @ McCormick's
description:
This is an EMERGENCY! Senate Protest Event in Philadelphia Continues This Week and For the Foreseeable Future.

Now called "Monday's at McCormick's" each Monday at noon - rain or shine - Here's why:

We are living in a MAGA-republican Coup. We were warned. Now it's here!

Here at home our democratic rights are being eroded and the Trump/Musk team is putting us all in danger. The limits of Executive power against the courts are being tested every day. If Trump decides to ignore the courts, there is very little they can do to enforce their decisions and unless Congress acts, it would be a true constitutional crisis. (And so far, Congress is controlled by the MAGA movement and the Democrats have not done enough to stand up and fight back.) It could even spiral down into outright civil war as competing factions and states careen between untested solutions to protect their own interests and those of their constituents and funders. There is real harm being done across the entire domestic sector. Layoffs, program cuts for the needy and for the average US resident, persecution of law abiding immigrants and students and other activists for simply speaking their mind and organizing constitutionally protected protest. Fear is also their weapon.

Our international role is being flipped on its head - yes, the US has always had a questionable foreign policy, providing aid and promoting democracy and human rights - to a degree - on the one hand, while at the same time invading other countries for the good of corporate profits and geopolitical dominance. Trump considers a policy to outright invade counties like Mexico and Greenland in violation of international law and to extend US power - A clear expression of Empire! Trump is considering power grabs not unlike those that the Nazi regime in Germany perpetrated in search of "Lebensraum", (Living Space) a euphemism for territorial conquest. And they got away with it (for a while) because the people who stood up were either jailed, exiled or murdered. The rest were either regime supporters (Like the solid 30% base of the MAGA movement) or went along out of fear of retribution. We cannot let fear prevent us from standing up this time. History will judge us.

We now have a true oligarchy in the US and we must fight back!

The Trump administration’s illegal actions and relentless efforts to dismantle protections for vulnerable communities — both here in the U.S. and abroad— have made clear we are in the midst of an authoritarian takeover not unlike what has happened in Orban’s Hungary. 

His plan to "Own Gaza" and move out Palestinians is NOT a plan to destroy Hamas and increase Israeli security - it is ETHNIC CLEANSING pure and simple. It's a land grab. All for development rights and to secure a seaport access to natural gas deposits off the shore of Gaza in the Mediterranean Sea. The Levant gas field includes the shores of historic Palestine (Israel and Gaza), Syria, Lebanon and, on the opposite side, the island of Cyprus. This field is estimated to contain about 122 trillion cubic feet of natural gas. So it will accelerate the climate emergency. 

As we all know Trump/Musk plan to get rid of a number of government agencies that protect our health, livelihood and constitutional rights. - the EPA is on the hit list. The Department of Education is too. So, is the CDC, the NIH and many other important agencies that protect the US public.

As we all know - thousands have already been fired, causing chaos and havoc and real harm to both dedicated civil servants AND people served by life affirming programs voted on by the U.S. people and enacted, in most cases, by the U.S. Congress. The Administration may have authority to make staffing decisions, but as is the case with the Department of Education - many of these agencies can only be eliminated by acts of Congress - Trump has overstepped his legal authority.

Thankfully, the courts have, so far, acted as a check on much of Trumps clear and blatant abuses of executive power. But we cannot count on the courts, particularly the US Supreme court, which has been stacked by Trump appointees and ideologues friendly to executive power. 

Resistance is NOT futile - it is essential. 

We are launching "Monday's at McCormick's" each Monday at noon - rain or shine - we will assemble peaceably - as is our constitutional right - outside Senator McCormick's Philadelphia office until Senator McCormick agrees to meet with us and support our demands: (These will change as conditions develop)

 1 - Stop voting for legislation inspired by Trump's project 2025 agenda - a plan to slash Medicaid, gut school lunch programs, and shut down nursing homes while handing more power to billionaires like Elon Musk. 

2- Roll back Trump's mean spirited and Unconstitutional funding pauses. Shutting down USAID is already killing people in need all over the World. Cuts to programs here in the US could do the same. Funding for these programs are up to the Congress and the US people to decide, not Trump! 

That's just for starters. Overall we want Senator McCormick to represent us all, not just his rich friends. We want Senator McCormick to DO HIS JOB!
The stakes could not be higher. The administration is pushing an authoritarian agenda that threatens our democracy, our rights, and the well-being of millions here at home and around the planet. 

We have the power to resist—and we must use every tool at our disposal to stop them.

Bring your creative celebratory energy--wear red, white and/or blue, brings flags, No Kings signs, bells, kazoos, drums, etc. During our action, please observe and support each other, stay on the sidewalks on either side of State Street with your signs not extending into the street. title: Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks: Put Quad Cities Families Over Billionaires
description:
Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks is expected to vote once again to gut Medicaid, defund public education, and slash housing programs — all while protecting tax breaks for billionaires and large corporations.

We already know where she stands — and we’re not waiting quietly.

Join us for a public rally and press conference outside her office to hold her accountable for choosing billionaires over families in the Quad Cities.

📍Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks Davenport Office, 201 W 2nd St Suite 705 Davenport, Iowa 52801
📅 Tuesday, July 8th
⏰ 12PM - 1PM

This is about our health care, our schools, our homes — and the choices she keeps making against us.

We’re calling on neighbors, advocates, and everyday Quad Cities residents to show up and say: Enough is enough.

Rep. Miller-Meeks does not get to make these cuts without facing the people impacted.

title: Save Our Libraries
description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Indivisible McHenry County is hosting a protest rally to show our opposition to the Trump administration's proposed elimination of the IMLS (Institute of Museum and Library Services), which will affect us on a local level. The rally will take place on Friday, June 20th, in front of the McHenry Public Library, 809 Front St (Rte 31), McHenry, from 3 p.m. until 5 p.m.

On June 6th, a Federal judge gave the Trump administration permission to proceed with dismantling the IMLS even though there is another lawsuit underway that is trying to save the agency through a different Federal court.

The IMLS was created and funded by Congress in 1996 for the purpose of providing support to libraries and museums in every state in the U.S. The agency has had bipartisan support throughout its history, with reauthorization occurring under the Clinton, George W. Bush, Obama, and Trump administrations. The IMLS is required by law to conduct activities that support libraries and to provide reports to Congress on important issues. The devastating cuts to the IMLS’s grants and services will make it impossible for the agency to operate as required by Congress. 

Although libraries in McHenry County do not rely on the IMLS for most of their funding, the elimination of the IMLS could still result in cuts to library services that are enjoyed by our residents and tens of thousands of other people in Illinois. The IMLS provides millions of dollars in funding to the Illinois State Library that is used to fund RAILS (Reaching Across Illinois Libraries System), the government agency that assists more than 4000 library facilities in Illinois, including all of the libraries in McHenry County.

RAILS provides the interlibrary delivery service which allows library patrons to check out books and other items from any library within the Illinois system. RAILS also provides: a shared electronic catalog and cataloging support • group purchases and member discounts that helps libraries to save money • continuing education and consulting resources to library employees and trustees • content services for online publishing • grant opportunities for local libraries • and many other valuable services. If the IMLS is eliminated it is unlikely that RAILS will be able to survive, and all of the valuable services that it provides to our residents will also be eliminated. Let your voice be heard. Please join us on June 20th.
